data.name: Rabbitfolk
data.description:
Rabbitfolk are a resilient subrace of the Chimera, predominantly hailing from the slums of Northi and Westria. Historically looked down on by the Catfolk, they continue to face prejudice from some older-minded individuals who view them as inferior. Rabbitfolk often have incredibly large families and very deep ties to community and to support themselves, they tend to take on less desirable jobs throughout the city. It is not uncommon for entire businesses to be run by extended families of Rabbitfolk or by joint community ventures. Due to this focus on family and community, Rabbitfolk tend to create very strong bonds with any companions they spend long periods of time with. It is not unheard of for long-time coworkers, school friends, or adventuring companions to suddenly find themselves as “part of the family” and inducted into an expansive extended family. However, despite their industrious nature, persistent social stigma has driven many Rabbitfolk to seek alternative means of livelihood, sometimes turning to crime as a desperate measure to ensure their families' well-being.

At the helm of Mothergreen's infamous Lorenz Mafia is Fiona MacCocairy, a determined Rabbitfolk girl who strives to bring honor to the underworld. Fiona has initiated a battle of optics, working tirelessly to clean up the Mafia and institute strict codes of honor, thereby bringing a semblance of respect and legitimacy to even their criminal trade. Her efforts highlight the tragic reality that many Rabbitfolk's involvement in crime stems from a profound desire to provide for their loved ones at any cost. Playing a Rabbitfolk is ideal for players who wish to embody characters with large, extended families, expansive communities, and explore the underworld and adverse conditions.

Size: Medium

data.name: Raijin
data.description:
Raijin are an exceptionally rare subrace of Youkai, embodying the very essence of lightning crystallized into sentient form. Their bodies are conduits of electrical energy, with vibrant arcs of lightning coursing through and emanating around them, granting them an electrifying presence that is both mesmerizing and formidable. Possessing incredible speed and agility, Raijin can catch and consume lightning, harnessing its raw power to fuel their abilities and enhance their combat prowess. This mastery over electrical energy not only makes them swift and lethal on the battlefield but also allows them to manipulate their surroundings with bursts of lightning-infused magic. Due to the intense energy that flows through and around them, Raijin often feel uncomfortable amidst the energetic fields of their own kind, which compels them to lead solitary lives.

Historically, Raijin have traversed the farthest and most remote reaches of Lyr, their nomadic lifestyles a testament to their independence and relentless pursuit of personal goals. On the battlefield, Raijin excel as lone warriors or as leaders of small, focused units, utilizing their incredible energy to wipe out enemies in single combat. Their unique abilities allow them to absorb lightning, rendering them impervious to such assaults, and to imbue their weapons with crackling electricity, transforming them into fearsome instruments of battle. This dual mastery not only enhances their offensive capabilities but also instills fear in their adversaries. While typically solitary, Raijin can bring tactical advantages to an adventuring party, wreathing their weapons in electricity for a powerful frontal assault. Players who thrive as lone wolves and enjoy infusing weapons with power, will find playing a Raijin immensely rewarding. Additionally, those who aspire to lead or prefer to follow their own desires without hesitation will resonate with the Raijin's independent and dynamic nature, making them captivating and influential allies.

Size: Medium

data.name: Ratfolk
data.description:
Ratfolk are a versatile subrace of the Chimera, seamlessly integrated into all walks of life throughout the vast lands of Lyr. Found all over from the bustling cities like Westria to the expansive plains of Axias, Ratfolk are renowned for their exceptional adaptability and resourcefulness. Their prehensile tails grant them unparalleled dexterity, making them adept laborers and specialists in performing a wide array of odd jobs. Whether working as carpenters in the city, or tracking down dungeons as adventurers, they can be found living their day to day lives with a sense of purpose, taking it one day at a time. Ratfolk are agile experts being incredibly hard to catch. Despite their presence in diverse environments, Ratfolk maintain a strong sense of community through large family units, though they often venture out to pursue individual endeavors, returning periodically to reunite with their kin.

Playing a Ratfolk means embodying a character that excels in versatility and everyday practicality. Ideal for players who enjoy characters skilled in various tasks and adept at handling diverse challenges, Ratfolk bring a unique blend of hardworking efficiency and laid-back charm to any adventuring party. Their ability to perform multiple roles with ease makes them invaluable in both combat and non-combat scenarios, while their relaxed demeanor fosters a harmonious and approachable presence within the group. Whether taking on the role of a diligent craftsman, a cunning scout, or a dependable support character, Ratfolk offer players the opportunity to create relatable and multifaceted personas. For those seeking to portray a character that balances productivity with a relaxed, everyday person feel, Ratfolk are the perfect choice, adding practicality to an adventuring party.

Size: Small

data.name: Red Pandafolk
data.description:
Red Pandas are a solitary subrace of Chimera, renowned for their ability to seamlessly integrate into diverse cultures across the expansive realm of Lyr. Unlike other races that form tight-knit communities, Red Pandas prefer to forge individual paths, often immersing themselves in the societies they inhabit rather than clustering with their kin. Their aloof and relaxed demeanor masks a deep-seated competence, as they approach every task with a lightheartedness that not only enhances their own resilience but also uplifts the morale of those around them. This carefree attitude does not diminish their effectiveness; rather, it complements their exceptional agility and acrobatic prowess, making them elusive and unpredictable in both social interactions and combat scenarios.

Despite their easygoing nature, Red Pandas are inherently cautious and can be easily spooked, a trait that paradoxically transforms them into formidable fighters. Their heightened awareness and instinctual fear responses enable them to navigate and survive even the most perilous situations with remarkable dexterity and strategic finesse. Those who underestimate the Red Panda's seemingly detached attitude often find themselves outmaneuvered and defeated by these slippery warriors. In gameplay, Red Pandas are ideal for players who wish to embody characters that have a "my pace" attitude, utilizing their acrobatic skills and evasive techniques to outsmart opponents. Embracing a Red Panda character offers a unique blend of aloof charm and combat versatility, providing both strategic advantages and a dynamic presence.

Size: Medium

data.name: Ryujin
data.description:
Ryujin are a rare and prideful sub-race of Youkai with distinctive draconic features. Claiming to be the only true direct descendants of mythical dragons, Ryujin are often at odds with Lizardfolk and Kobolds, who both claim the same - though Ryujin don’t give the opinions of “lesser races” much thought in that regard. Overall, Ryujin are regal and intimidating with a presence that commands a room and a glare that can silence a crowd.

Culturally, Ryujin live together and apart from the rest of Kiraran society. They don’t tend to form Ryujin villages but instead take on leadership roles in other Youkai communities as exclusive merchants, mayors, governors, or just wealthy nobles leveraging their wealth and power. They demand a level of excellence from those around them that causes communities they’re in to both be free of corruption and require full, constant effort of improvement that can drive people away in search for an easier, simpler life.

But what Ryujin demand of others, they demand of themselves even more intensely. Ryujin craftsmen will spend decades perfecting a single work to be worthy of their effort and lineage. Warriors will master techniques passed down from master to student for hundreds of years and often fight with an elegance that would be more at home on a stage than a battlefield. Scholars and mages dissect and understand their chosen fields to degrees of minutia reserved for specialist universities. Striking up a conversation about a Ryujin’s interest will be a sure method of being regaled with the proper impact angles for hammering the shape of a katana, an arcane breakdown of individual elements of the Glittershard spell, or a detailed retelling down to individual combatants of an ancient, obscure battle.

But most mysterious of all are Ryujin adventurers. Often young and still in training (for a Ryujin), their drive to seek out the wonders of the world is second to none. The pride and drive for excellence is still present but there is often an underlying goal or purpose in their traveling the world. Ryujin adventurers are often knowledgeable in history and lost knowledge and they always seem to be searching for something, an ancient item or manuscript or tome. Unless you are extremely close to a Ryujin, it is not recommended to press them on the details of their search.

“You are ignorant of what stands before you.”

Size: Medium

But what Ryujin demand of others, they demand of themselves even more intensely. Ryujin craftsmen will spend decades perfecting a single work to be worthy of their effort and lineage. Warriors will master techniques passed down from master to student for hundreds of years and often fight with an elegance that would be more at home on a stage than a battlefield. Scholars and mages dissect and understand their chosen fields to degrees of minutia reserved for specialist universities. Striking up a conversation about a Ryujin’s interest will be a sure method of being regaled with the proper impact angles for hammering the shape of a katana, an arcane breakdown of individual elements of the Glittershard spell, or a detailed retelling down to individual combatants of an ancient, obscure battle.

But most mysterious of all are Ryujin adventurers. Often young and still in training (for a Ryujin), their drive to seek out the wonders of the world is second to none. The pride and drive for excellence is still present but there is often an underlying goal or purpose in their traveling the world. Ryujin adventurers are often knowledgeable in history and lost knowledge and they always seem to be searching for something, an ancient item or manuscript or tome. Unless you are extremely close to a Ryujin, it is not recommended to press them on the details of their search.

“You are ignorant of what stands before you.”

data.name: Salamander
data.description:
Salamanders are a proud, fiercely independent race, valuing personal strength and mastery over their innate fire magic. They are artisans at heart, channeling their elemental gifts into crafts that demand intense heat and fine control, such as metalwork, glassblowing, and the forging of enchanted items. In Sorthen, where these arts are highly respected, Salamanders have carved out a niche for themselves as master crafters, known for producing items of rare beauty and resilience.

While they have a somewhat insular culture, valuing Salamander kinship and traditions, they are not unwelcoming to outsiders. In Glassteps, their primary settlement, Salamanders coexist harmoniously with Demons and other races.

Salamander society places a strong emphasis on self-expression through craft. Each Salamander seeks to leave a mark on the world through their creations, which often hold personal or spiritual significance. Their apprenticeships are long and arduous, as young Salamanders must learn to temper their fiery nature and master their powers before they are considered full artisans. This mastery is symbolized by the ritual creation of a “Soulforge,” a unique piece of art that captures the essence of the Salamander’s inner fire and serves as a testament to their skill and control.

Size: Medium

Winner of the 2023 Alpha Race Creation Contest (Elementals) by Sabbrewolf.

data.name: Selkie
data.description:
Selkies are mesmerizing Aquatic Fae primarily found off the tranquil shores of Houkaina, where their presence enriches the vibrant merfolk society. Although relatively rare, many Selkies have become prominent members of Houkaina, contributing significantly to its cultural and magical tapestry. While a majority of Selkies cherish their seaside abodes, a notable number venture beyond the coast, establishing homes near rivers or lakes to remain close to their beloved water sources. This preference for aquatic environments underscores their deep connection to water, allowing them to seamlessly integrate into various aquatic communities and adapt to both marine and freshwater realms. Central to Selkie identity is the magic seal cloak, a precious item bestowed upon them at birth, much like the Tengu. This cloak grants Selkies the ability to transform into their elusive Seal Form, a transformation shrouded in mystery as it remains unclear whether the seal form or their humanoid appearance came first. In their Seal Form, Selkies exhibit extraordinary speed and agility underwater, making them nearly impossible to capture and allowing them to navigate the depths with unparalleled grace.

A defining cultural aspect of the Selkies is the profound significance of their seal cloaks. According to longstanding oral traditions, if a person were to steal a Selkie's cloak, the Selkie is culturally obligated to marry them. Although this obligation is not enforced by law, many Selkies take this tradition seriously, fiercely protecting their sealskin cloaks from theft—with many learning magic methods at an early age to summon and protect this cloak.  Additionally, Selkies possess the innate ability to infuse water with their own mana, enabling them to manipulate it for various magical applications, which makes them exceptional Hydromancers and Cryomancers. Their early mastery of spells related to hiding and summoning their magic items further enhances their mystical prowess. Players who choose to play a Selkie character will appreciate the blend of aquatic grace and magical versatility, making Selkies ideal for those who wish to explore the freedom of the ocean and mystery of an aquatic Fae society.

Size: Medium

data.name: Sheepfolk
data.description:
Sheepfolk are a sub-race of Chimera, native to the plains and lake coastline of what is now southern Axias, most sheepfolk now live in the plains area within Northi between Axias and Eisenstadt. Born with a natural sensitivity to magic, Sheepfolk have historically built settlements and migrated along major leylines. They were of critical help to sages in mapping and studying these invisible rivers of magical energy and many airship captains today feel it is good luck to have a sheepfolk on board. This deep sensitivity to magic comes from unique spirit circuits linked to their hair follicles, allowing unprecedented detection ability to magical energies and signals. Additionally, this sensitivity (and the natural talent to send magical signals as well) allows a sheepfolk to sense and smooth away the chaotic magical rhythm of physical exhaustion and mental fatigue. It’s said that the best night sleep a person can get is in the arms of or resting on the lap of a sheepfolk.

However, this magical sensitivity made sheepfolk uniquely useful in one very critical field: communications. With their innate ability to sense and send magical signals, they are commonly hired, trained, or conscripted into militaries. Historically, the use of sheepfolk and advancing artifice communication technology allowed Northi to dominate conflicts with accurate maneuver warfare. Only the overwhelming might of Westrian paladins and the scouting and aerial advantages of the demon aerial mages prevented Northi domination of the peninsula in full. This paradigm nearly changed radically during the Four Swords War. Sheepfolk communication specialists began utilizing new jamming artifices. Not only were these specialists key in continuing Northi’s domination of communication range and quality, but they were also able to use these new tools to isolate Sorthen communication signals and adaptively jam them. This removal of critical communication ability combined with the joint strike with Westrian forces and newly implemented aeromancers finally allowed the demons to be pushed back.

A major setback in the conflict drew the attention of sheepfolk after the war’s conclusion. Somehow, someway, the demons had briefly established completely untraceable and secure communications between their command posts in the south and their last general in the field. This limited communication allowed the demons to organize a blocking action at the Battle of Three Passes where General Ar’Golan’s battalion was able to hold back the invasion for weeks, allowing the evacuation of the remaining demon forces to Marlone Bay. This feat, which suddenly failed at the end of the battle, was investigated and the work of Aetherie Lu’Pana was discovered. Since the end of the war, the techniques and technology of the Aetherie has spread like a blaze through the sheepfolk communities, building on and allowing them to improve their own innate abilities to levels they’d never gone before. It is commonly thought among the sheepfolk that the late Aetherie Lu’Pana must have had sheepfolk help or had studied sheepfolk extensively to develop what she had.

Sheepfolk adventurers are often quiet, having grown up where needing to speak up to be heard was unnecessary, and they tend to shy away from those who are loud (both in actual volume and in showing off their magical energy). They will also think it is quite normal for groups to request them to act as a communication hub, even among new parties or strangers. But their comforting embrace and comfortable dreams are only for friends.

Size: Medium

data.name: Slimefolk
data.description:
Slimefolk are a rare subrace of Chimera, tracing their lineage back to slime creatures that inhabit every corner of Lyr. Despite their gelatinous origins, Slimefolk possess a humanoid form that mirrors their unique personalities, and while this can change over time, it cannot be willingly altered without great strain and training. To better integrate into diverse societies and mitigate the unsettling responses to the nature of their true forms, many Slimefolk's first exposure to magic is a basic glamour spell, allowing them to seamlessly blend in and navigate social landscapes with ease.

Highly independent by nature, Slimefolk typically do not form tight-knit communities with other Slimefolk, largely due to their rarity and solitary tendencies. While they do not possess an inherent sex, Slimefolk have developed the ability to emulate sexual characteristics to facilitate social interactions and relationships. Their exceptional ability to blend into any society means that others often perceive them as members of different, more humanoid races, unaware of their true slimy heritage. This chameleon-like quality makes Slimefolk ideal for players who wish to navigate complex social environments undetected, while also having access to unique techniques that can surprise and outmaneuver others when needed. Embracing a Slimefolk character means valuing independence and adaptability, offering both strategic advantages and a versatile role.

Size: Medium

To better integrate into diverse societies and mitigate the unsettling responses to the nature of their true forms, many Slimefolk's first exposure to magic is a basic glamour spell, allowing them to seamlessly blend in and navigate social landscapes with ease.Highly independent by nature, Slimefolk typically do not form tight-knit communities with other Slimefolk, largely due to their rarity and solitary tendencies. While they do not possess an inherent sex, Slimefolk have developed the ability to emulate sexual characteristics to facilitate social interactions and relationships. Their exceptional ability to blend into any society means that others often perceive them as members of different, more humanoid races, unaware of their true slimy heritage. This chameleon-like quality makes Slimefolk ideal for players who wish to navigate complex social environments undetected, while also having access to unique techniques that can surprise and outmaneuver others when needed. Embracing a Slimefolk character means valuing independence and adaptability, offering both strategic advantages and a versatile role.Size: Medium

data.name: Spiderfolk
data.description:
Spiderfolk are a unique and industrious subrace of the Chimera, descended from ground spiders that mutated into a more humanoid direction. Their multiple arms enhance their dexterity, making them exceptional at multitasking and performing a wide array of tasks simultaneously. While they do not naturally use webs beyond utility purposes, a few Spiderfolk have trained to imbue their webs with mana, transforming them into incredibly durable tools for combat and defense.

In the heart of Northi City, Spiderfolk often purchase small, seemingly uninhabitable plots of land and build their homes vertically, creating spider houses that are architectural marvels with furniture often bolted sideways into the walls. Many Spiderfolk are renowned as masterful chefs, such as Master Chef Vinia Lalune, who runs Northi's most luxurious restaurant, "Silk And Kettle." Her culinary creations have earned her widespread acclaim, showcasing the Spiderfolk's exceptional multitasking abilities in the kitchen. Players who wish to embody characters skilled in object interaction and vertical gameplay, will find Spiderfolk to be an ideal choice. 

Size: Medium

data.name: Suryan
data.description:
Suryan are a secluded sub-race of Youkai. Often described as “light given form”, the radiance that surrounds them is unmistakable and they are a spectacle for those who have never seen a Suryan before. Most Suryan are deeply spiritual and hold a reverence for light and its nurturing properties.

Suryan villages and towns tend to be located in high mountain valleys, as close to the sun as can be managed while still able to support crops. The warm light each Suryan gives off makes their villages pleasantly welcoming and even the most inhospitable seeming locations team with trees, farms, and wildlife due to their influence. It is not uncommon to scale a frigid mountain pass only to descend into a shallow valley full of warm sunlight and green nature fully at odds with the surrounding mountains.

These villages and towns often support mountaintop monasteries where Suryan monks learn and meditate on the Five Harmonies, with the first and oldest, Divyajyotiḥ Ālayaḥ, being located in a secluded section of the Nāganṛtya Parvataḥ placed upon the highest peak, Nīlāmbaraśikharaḥ. Five Harmonies monasteries produce revered wisdoms and graceful healers and are common pilgrimages for the wealthy and destitute alike.

Suryan adventurers carry that spirituality and sense of community with them on their journeys. While not all will be mystical monks capable of weaving light into healing threads, their willingness to help even in small ways is a common behavior. A Suryan adventurer is just as comfortable clearing the wilderness of dangerous monsters as they are cheerfully helping a farmer harvest their crops. Many Suryan have been taught from a young age the basic mysticism of Five Harmonies as a guiding principle, although those born and raised outside of those mountain communities may lack that connection.

Expect Suryan companions to be spiritual and compassionate to those around them.

“Jīvanaḥ jyotibhiḥ jāyate. All life springs from light.”

TL Notes:

Nāganṛtya Parvataḥ - The Mountains of the Dragon Dance

Nīlāmbaraśikharaḥ - The Blue-Robed Peak, in this case blue-robed is a poetic epithet for the sky. 

Divyajyotiḥ Ālayaḥ - The Sanctuary of Divine Light

Size: Medium

data.name: Sylph
data.description:
The Sylph are a subrace of Fae that are particularly blessed by the Wind. Said to have been born of the breeze that danced through the branches and leaves of Yggdrasil herself, there are no beings on Lyr that are more attuned to the wind than a Sylph. To the Sylph, the sky and the wind are their natural companions and hold all the joys and secrets of the world.

Sylph villages and cities are built high in the treetops of Easter, wrapping naturally around the massive ancient trees and they rarely have any way of accessing them without flight. These villages can be uncomfortable for visitors as they sway and flex naturally with the trees they’re a part of. The hovering farms are one of the many spectacles of their villages, unique vertical farmland suspended high above the forest floor and are the only place Starlight Berries can be grown, one of the most coveted fruits in Easter.

With their close connection to the sky, Sylph’s first developed the method to pluck stars from above as Starcallers, although they rarely used these skills for harm. Sylph Starcallers are the centerpiece for all manner of celebrations in Easter, providing a spectacle of falling starlight that not even the most elaborate fireworks displays of Kirara can rival.

Sylph adventurers tend to be free spirits, enamored with exploration and discovering all the ways the wind can rush over the stones or twist through distant forests. They have long traditions of archery and agile swordsmanship and they often scoff at the proclaimed control aeromancers boast over the wind and delight in watching their supposed master of the winds fail in the face of the Blessing of Wind.

Sylph companions can be trusted to be skilled and focused in their chosen profession although they can sometimes be distracted by an interesting curl of wind through the leaves.

Size: Medium

data.name: Tengu
data.description:
Tengu are a distinguished subrace of Youkai, recognizable as humanoids adorned with majestic wings that grant them the ability to soar through the skies of Lyr. Originating from the rugged mountains of Mt. Merlin, Tengu reside alongside the dangerous Astra Line, a region teeming with chaotic astra energy and perilous creatures known as Fiends. Each Tengu possesses the unique ability to summon a supernatural mask, meticulously crafted to reflect their individual essence. When donned, these masks suppress their innate aura and presence, rendering them nearly invisible to magical detection. This ability is crucial for their survival, as it allows them to navigate the treacherous landscapes at the border of the Astra Line undetected by the ever-present threat of Fiends. Renowned as fierce warriors and specialist Fiend hunters, they have developed the technique of bathing their weapons in their own aura.  This specialty technique creating properties similar to silver weapons to shatter Fiendish defenses. Tengu play a pivotal role in safeguarding their homeland and by proxy the homelands of others, maintaining the delicate balance between order and chaos.

Despite many Tengu villages falling under the jurisdiction of Northi, the kingdom respects their autonomy, recognizing the invaluable protection Tengu provide by keeping Fiends at bay. This mutual respect fosters a harmonious relationship, with the citizens of Northi viewing the presence of Tengu as a blessing rather than a burden. Tengu society is built on principles of strength, honor, and resilience, making them ideal companions for those who seek to embody the spirit of a fierce slayer. Players who are drawn to characters that harness the power of flight, excel in combat, and specialize in hunting formidable monsters will find the Tengu subrace exceptionally rewarding. Embracing a Tengu character means stepping into the role of a vigilant protector, capable of swift aerial maneuvers and specialist knowledge of Fiends, guiding the party's path against the most evil of creatures.

Size: Medium

data.name: Unseelie
data.description:
The Unseelie are a feared and infamous branch of the Fae, marked by their dark complexions, dagger-thin features, and eyes that shimmer like oil in moonlight. The Unseelie dwell in eternal gloom, deep in the heart of the Eastern Forests where sunlight never reaches, and where even other Fae dare not tread.

Unseelie society is one of discipline, cruelty, and control. Though they rarely harm each other, their reputation for depravity is well-earned. They take great pride in the art of suffering, perfecting pain as both punishment and expression. Captives brought into the dark woods are not killed quickly, if at all. They are kept, their torment prolonged by methods that are as surgical as they are sadistic. To the Unseelie, mercy is wasteful, and empathy is an affliction to be corrected.

Despite this darkness, or perhaps because of it, Unseelie adventurers are not rare. They often leave the forest not out of exile, but ambition. In the wider world, their talents for interrogation, infiltration, and assassination find both fear and value. While some become little more than thugs or enforcers, others integrate into adventuring parties, happy to do the "dirty work" others shy from. 

Unseelie adventurers gravitate toward melee combat, preferring to witness an enemy’s suffering from up close, though many also learn some form of healing. They typically excel at sabotage, torture, and covert operations. Unseelie also generally have no moral restrictions and will use whatever tactic ensures victory.

While some Unseelie may suppress their darker instincts, most do not apologize for what they are. Those who travel with an Unseelie should always keep that in mind, lest they find themselves with a dagger in the back.

“Death is not punishment. It is a mercy.”

Size: Medium

Though they rarely harm each other, their reputation for depravity is well-earned. They take great pride in the art of suffering, perfecting pain as both punishment and expression. Captives brought into the dark woods are not killed quickly, if at all. They are kept, their torment prolonged by methods that are as surgical as they are sadistic. To the Unseelie, mercy is wasteful, and empathy is an affliction to be corrected.Despite this darkness, or perhaps because of it, Unseelie adventurers are not rare. They often leave the forest not out of exile, but ambition. In the wider world, their talents for interrogation, infiltration, and assassination find both fear and value. While some become little more than thugs or enforcers, others integrate into adventuring parties, happy to do the "dirty work" others shy from. Unseelie adventurers gravitate toward melee combat, preferring to witness an enemy’s suffering from up close, though many also learn some form of healing. They typically excel at sabotage, torture, and covert operations. Unseelie also generally have no moral restrictions and will use whatever tactic ensures victory.While some Unseelie may suppress their darker instincts, most do not apologize for what they are. Those who travel with an Unseelie should always keep that in mind, lest they find themselves with a dagger in the back.“Death is not punishment. It is a mercy.”Size: Medium
data.Abilities: Darkvision (passive); Elemental Mastery: Dark; Torture Techniques

data.name: Willo Wisp
data.description:
Willo Wisps are mischievous faeries of light, known for their playful nature and enchanting presence within the forests of Lyr. Primarily nocturnal, these elusive beings possess the innate ability to emit and manipulate light, creating mesmerizing displays that captivate all who witness them. While most Willo Wisps thrive under the cover of darkness, a select few have adapted to living during the daytime, blending their luminous abilities with the natural light to remain hidden yet active. Their strong connection with Faerie Light Eyes grants them the power to weave intricate illusions, allowing them to strike at the minds of their targets and manipulate perceptions with ease. Historically, before relations between the Fae and other races improved, many adventurers who dared to explore the Eastern forests were lured to their doom by Willo Wisps. Those unfortunate souls whose eyes met the fiery blue glow of activated Faerie Light Eyes were ensnared in illusions, guiding them toward their deaths to never be seen again.

Despite the legends and cautionary tales passed down through generations, Willo Wisps themselves harbor no ill will toward these prejudices; in fact, many revel in the fear and mystery surrounding them. Stories among Human and Chimera alike continue to warn children against venturing into the woods at night, lest a Willo Wisp lead them to an early demise. This enigmatic behavior adds a layer of allure and intrigue to the Willo Wisps, making them a compelling choice for players who wish to embody a race with inherent magical eye powers or embody the classic mischievous fae who delight in the fearful tales spun about them.

Size: Small

data.name: Wolf-folk
data.description:
Wolf-folk are a distinguished subrace of Chimera, inhabiting the rugged snowy peaks of Mt. Merlin and extending their presence to the vast expanses of Susururu Forest, where the largest populations thrive. These resilient beings have developed a predatory instinct that enables them to meticulously hone in on and swiftly eliminate their prey, striking decisively when they detect any sign of weakness. Renowned as some of the finest hunters in the realm, Wolf-folk sustain themselves by thriving on nature's bounty, establishing and maintaining small, tightly-knit villages among their own kind. Their exceptional hunting prowess is complemented by their remarkable teamwork; Wolf-folk excel in collaborating with trusted allies, skillfully exploiting any openings their companions create to maximize their effectiveness in both combat and survival scenarios.

The hunting skill of Wolf-folk is highly esteemed, particularly their animal furs, which are considered the best in the realm. These furs are meticulously prepared and sought after by merchants who journey to the remote, forested, and mountainous villages where Wolf-folk reside. The quality and durability of their furs make them invaluable commodities, enhancing the reputation of Wolf-folk artisans across Lyr. Despite their isolated habitats, the Wolf-folk maintain a robust network of trade and interaction with outside merchants, ensuring that their villages remain prosperous and their skills highly regarded. Players that want to play keen hunters who work well with others would enjoy what Wolf-folk have to offer.

Size: Medium

data.name: Yuki-Onna
data.description:
Yuki-Onna are an rare subrace of Youkai, exclusively female snow spirits who embody the serene yet formidable essence of winter. Primarily inhabiting the frigid regions around Mt. Merlin, the eastern fringes of Easter's forest, and the vast expanses of the Mirane Tundra, Yuki-Onna live in tightly-knit tribes that reflect their deep connection to their icy environments. These Youkai are incredibly rare outside their snowy homelands, with only those possessing powerful soul cores daring to traverse into warmer climates. In the magical sanctuary of Kirara, a sizeable population of Yuki-Onna thrives, thanks to the strong ambient magic that allows them to withstand the heat. Their presence in Kirara not only highlights their resilience but also their drive to adapt to different climates.

Yuki-Onna are renowned for their mastery of cryomancy, a powerful form of magic that allows them to control and manipulate ice and snow. This mastery was exemplified by the legendary cryomancer, Mirane, who was mentored by the Tsurara tribe of Yuki-Onna in the creation of the Eternal Mirane Cage—a legendary-class spell. Following the sealing of a dangerous Fiend by Mirane, Yuki-Onna played a crucial role in the subsequent expedition to eliminate the threat, showcasing their prowess as fierce warriors and reliable allies. Playing a Yuki-Onna is ideal for players who relish the roles of outsiders and travelers, embracing characters who navigate the world with grace despite its hostility. Their unique abilities and tribal heritage offer a rich narrative experience, perfect for those seeking to portray resilient and independent spirits who are unafraid to journey far from home in pursuit of their goals.

Size: Medium

data.name: Chimera
data.description:
Chimera are creatures that have been mutated due to magic and have gained sentience.  Almost all Chimera can be traced back to areas of high magical concentration and a lifeform that was mutated.  Despite being quite varied in physical characteristics, all Chimera are effectively the same race at their core.  It is unknown how arcane magic was able to pattern itself in such a way…

From Slime Chimera to the more common Feline Chimeras, there are varied sub-races that can be found throughout the world. And those sub-races can vary widely, even within the same phenotypes. Coloration, ear and tail shapes, and even number of physical characteristics. These widely varying phenotypes are broadly categorized in two ways: kanolith and zoalith.

Kanolith chimera have limited physical characteristics. Most kanoliths will have ears, tails, or both corresponding to their sub-race. Kanoliths are the most common type of chimera overall and what most will think of when imagining a chimera of any sub-race.

Zoalith chimera have exaggerated or prevalent physical characteristics. Fur, scales, replaced or altered limbs, and animalistic face shapes are all examples of zoalith features. This often leads to zoalith chimera having a far more “bestial” appearance which can sometimes bring social challenges. While zoalith chimera are overall rarer than kanolith, there are some sub-races that this trend is reversed. Centaurs, harpies, lamiafolk, and slimefolk are all examples of sub-races which trend toward zoalith.
data.attributes: You gain +1 in toughness and +1 in awareness.
data.proficiencies: You can speak, read and write Common as well as the special dialect of your sub-race.
data.skills: You gain +5 skill points in either Magic, Survival, Animal Husbandry, Perception, Insight, Linguistics or Artifice.

data.name: Demon
data.description:
In Demon lore, they were the descendants of Angels who had rebelled against providence.  Losing their angelic wings and methods to absorb the Divine might of Light, they’ve adapted techniques to burn their own life force to temporarily tap into their powers.  The dangerous technique called Divine Release, is highly praised as the pinnacle of a demon’s powers.

While originally slandered as “demons” by humans and the angels of old, the demons have embraced the name as proof of their rebellion. 

Demons appear as humanoids, and but have varying secondary characteristics.  Some have tiny wings that are devoid of the providence absorbing “feathers”, while some have various kinds of horns or eye patterns.  Some even have pointed ears like the fae.

The Demon city of Sorthen exists as an aristocratic meritocracy, where the power balance shifts, houses die and new ones are born based on their contribution to society.  These Demon houses all grant their offspring a middle name, this name referencing their roles in society from servants to soldiers to scholars.  Each family passes down the techniques of their role, specializing for the greatest efficiency. None of these roles are looked down upon, and it is considered an honor to fulfill your purpose to the highest capability.  While the tradition of adhering to house societal roles, they are not inflexible.  It is not unusual for an individual to carve out a new life path if they demonstrate exceptional merit, and straying from that assigned family role would then not be viewed negatively.

Size: Medium
data.attributes: You gain +1 in Power and +1 in Reason.
data.proficiencies: You can speak, read, write Common and Sorthen.  You also gain proficiency in one common weapon or +5 skill points in a skill relating to your demon clan.
data.skills: You gain +5 skill points in either Common Knowledge, Magic, Religion, History, Flight, Artifice.

wi.text: Saboteurs - You gain proficiency with Saboteur Thread Daggers in addition to the ability below. You start with the Saboteur class unlocked and at level 1.

un.text: Maids and Butlers - You start with the Maid class unlocked and at level 1.

vi.text: Medical and Healers - You start with the Medic class unlocked and at level 1.

data.name: Fae
data.description:
The Fae are widely considered the first people that populated Lyra.  They are beings that were born from the will of nature and the world itself.  Faeries can be quite varied in culture and demeanor, some using their age immortality to achieve great wisdom-- while others might use it to laze about and be merry.

The most common type of Fae are the High Fae which appear as youthful humanoids with pointed ears and eyes that come in various colors and patterns

data.name: Human
data.description:
The origin of humans is not quite clear-- a race of generally homogenous characteristics in comparison to the other races.  Despite their similarity, humans are varied in nature and have adapted to many different environments.  Humans are quick learners and quick to adapt, a haste that is unseen in some of the other races, a byproduct of their generally shorter lifespans.

For a reason still unknown, the humans are blessed by providence-- the great power of divine light and are born with a special attunement for it regardless of their religion.

Size: Medium

data.name: Adjustable Lens Refractor Gun
data.description:
An artifice gun with cartridges that lets it fire blasts of arcane energy through a series of lenses rather than bullets. Attacks with this weapon deal Arcane damage. 

By spending 1 AP per lens, the user may adjust the strength of the gun at the cost of accuracy. Each lens adjusted for power lets the user treat their attacks with the weapon as if their power was 1 higher than it actually is, at the cost of their focus being treated as 1 lower than it actually is. Up to 3 lenses can be modified in this way. 

Exists in Musket and Sniper Rifle variants.

Mods:

Also takes normal musket and sniper rifle mods.

  • A mods:
    • Elemental Lens (10 points): Instead of Arcane, the weapon may deal a different element of your choosing
  • B mods:
    • None

data.name: Advanced Surgery Kit
data.description:
Surgery kits contain stitches, bandages and other items used for more serious wounds.

Rest Action: You perform minor surgery on an ally or yourself. Requires at least 5 points in Medicine (or a relevant expertise in Medicine) to use. Make a medicine check against DC 15. On success you can negate the effect of one injury suffered this campaign until the end of the campaign. An injury can only be negated once by this effect, and one person can only have one negated injury at a time.  The injury must still be dealt with after the campaign ends.

With an advanced surgery kit, you can heal two injuries from a single person instead of just one. The DC to heal two injuries is DC30.

data.name: Adventurer's Kit
data.description:
Adventuring kits contain all of the basic tools for adventuring. Included in the kit: Backpack, Flint and steel, Rope, Notebook, Pen, Compass, Bedroll, Torches, Hand Mirror.

Effect: You can use the items for their various purposes within reason. Can store up to 5 burden of Adventuring Essentials, a Northi Lantern or items included in this kit in a combat ready state for 0 burden and contains a torch/lantern holster for hands off torch/lantern use for light purposes. Cannot store kits or other burden reducing items in this combat ready state.

data.name: Aerial Staff (Custom Model)
data.description:
A custom model aerial staff has no fixed cost as it is made up from several parts. There are several base models that can be further modified through the use of parts.

Adding, removing or changing the parts of an aerial staff requires a level 8 artificer to spend an EP in town, though they may add and/or remove as many parts from a single staff as they want with that one EP.

For information on staves and how they work, check the rulebook.

All parts and staff models can be crafted by artificers and magitechnicians as if they were normal artifices. Unless stated otherwise, parts cannot be modified.

Unless stated otherwise, all aerial staff models have 3 burden, though this can be reduced with C mods like normal.

Models:


Falcon Model
Cost: 5000c
Slots:

  • Main Weapon S
  • Sub Weapon S
  • Sub Weapon S
  • Utility S
  • Utility S
  • Engine S


Egret Model
Cost: 5000c
Slots:

  • Main Weapon S
  • Sub Weapon S
  • Utility S
  • Utility S
  • Utility S
  • Engine S


Kestrel Model
Cost: 3000c
Slots:

  • Main Weapon S
  • Main Weapon S
  • Sub Weapon S
  • Engine S
Main Weapons

Sorthern Arc Buster Cannon
Ammo Capacity: 2. 1 Shell per use
Fixed Weapon, 0 RP, 60ft range, Strafe 50
You fire a blast of energy, making a heavy attack that deals arcane damage. This attack has the shieldbreaker property.
Cost: 1000c

Napalm Bomb
Ammo Capacity: 2. 1 Shell per use
Fixed Weapon, 0 RP, 90ft range, Strafe 25
You hurl a fireball at a 15x15ft area, making a Light attack that deals fire damage against all units in the area. On damage, you inflict Burning 5.
Cost: 750c

Sub Weapons

Magic Rocket Pods
Ammo Capacity: 2. 1 Shell per use
Turret Weapon, 0 RP, 30ft range
You fire a highly accurate blast of arcane energy at the target, making a Precise Attack that deals Arcane damage against the target. This attack has the Lock On property, but does not get pinpoint
Cost: 500c

Blaze Rifle
Gimballed Weapon, 120ft range, Strafe 10
Rapid, you make a Light (1 AP), Heavy (2 AP) or Precise (2 AP) attack against the target.
Cost: 1000c

Northi Gattling Rifle
Fixed Weapon, 30ft range, Strafe 50
1 AP, Make a light attack against the target and all targets 10ft directly behind it.
Cost: 500c

Sorthen Smoke Pod
Ammo Capacity: 1. 1 Shell per use
Turret Weapon, 0 RP, 30ft range
You create a sphere of smoke in a 15x15ft area that blocks line of sight. This effect functions similarly to Glittershards and lasts until the start of your next turn.
Cost: 1250c
 

Utility

Sorthen Shield Projector
Your staff gains a 25 HP shield. While the shield lasts, your staff does not lose altitude from any attacks that are made against the shield.
Cost: 1250c

Sorthen Ejection System
Ammo Capacity: 1. 1 Shell per use
0 RP, You immediately trigger wind bubble for both yourself and your artifice
Cost: 1000c

Medivac Rig
You can haul a downed ally on the underbelly of your staff, but your speed is halved while doing so.
Cost: 500c

Afterburner
Ammo Capacity: 1. 1 Shell per use
You double the speed of your staff for the next full movement action.
Cost: 1250c

Engine

Budget Model Engine
20ft air speed, no line movement. 1 Medium Shell per day.
Cost: 250c

Stock Model Engine
65ft air speed, 10ft turn. 1 Medium Shell per day
Cost: 750c

Arlan Custom Engine
35ft air speed, no line movement. 1 Medium Shell per day
Cost: 1500c

Wing Model Engine
50ft air speed, 30ft turn. 1 Medium Shell per day
Cost: 1000c

data.name: Aerial Staff (Sparrow Model)
data.description:
The Sparrow Model Aerial Staff design is the most simple entry level Aerial Staff.  It has a base speed of 20 feet and does not include integrated shielding or any weapon systems.  Often used for training, its fuel efficiency is fairly high. 

Its user can use it to fly. It has a speed of a 20ft.

Requires 1 hand to operate while flying.

Mods

  • A mods:
    • Jury-Rigged Cannon (10 points): Adds a small star cannon that fires an arcane blast from the front that deals heavy attack damage for 2 AP with 120ft Range. 
    • Medivac Rig (20 points): Allows a downed ally to be hauled on the underbelly of the staff. But reduces the speed by 10ft while hauling. 
    • Jury Rigged Shield (35 points): Adds a shield generator, granting the airship a 15 HP shield. This shield can be switched on and off, but can only be replenished by changing the fuel cell. 
  • B mods:
    • Sorthen Shield Generator (50 points): Requires Jury-Rigged Shield. Installs a Sorthen style Shield Generator increasing the shield value by 15 HP.
    • Upgraded Airship Engine (80 points): Increases the speed to 50ft but adds Line Movement: The airship may only move in a straight line when making a movement action.

    • Required extra's: 8x recipe's original cost.
    • Effect: +3 Crafting Dice

data.name: Anti-Air Weapon Sight
data.description:
An artifice designed to combat against aerial mages. Provides tracking assistance against the more predictable movement of air units. 

Attaches to ranged weapons. 

Increases the accuracy of ranged weapon attacks against flying targets by +4 until the start of your next turn.

Can be attached or detached by spending 4 AP.

Mods

  • A mods:
    • Holographic Optic (10 points): Increases the accuracy against flying targets by +1
  • B mods:
    • Wide Targeting (25 points): The accuracy bonus is reduced by 2, but it now works on all targets.
    • Aerial Targeting Mode (50 points): The effect now lasts until the end of the encounter or until deactivated by spending 2 AP. However, attacks against non-flying targets suffer a -4 penalty.
    • Wing Outlining (80 points): The first attack made after activation applies the downburst effect (See: Downburst ability)

data.name: Armor (Clothing)
data.description:
A high quality set of clothing. Does not provide any bonuses by itself, but if crafted by an armorsmith, can accept Flamellon mods.

Cannot be worn at the same time as regular armor.

Mods:

  • A mods
    • Mage Robes (20 points): You gain +1 maximum mana, but lose 1 guard and 2 block.
  • B mods
    • Cloud Robes (50 points): Your movement speed is increased by 5ft.
    • Battle Casting (80 points): The first spell you cast each turn does not provoke attacks of opportunity.
  • Frame mods
    • Reinforced Clothing (0 points): This clothing can benefit from material bonuses, but its burden is increased by 1.

data.name: Armor (Heavy)
data.description:
Increases your Guard by 3 and your Block by 12, but reduces your Initiative by 3 and your Evasion and Dodge by 6.

Mods

  • A mods:
    • Beacon Armor (35 points): Unarmored allies (except armor plates) within 40ft of you gain +1 guard.
  • B mods:
    • Deflecting Armor (25 points): An accuracy roll against you that rolls a 1 always misses.
    • Weighted Greaves (50 points): You become immovable while on the ground.
    • Titan Armor (50 points): You are treated as having a size category 1 step higher (maximum Large).
  • Frame mods:
    • Berserker Armor II (10 points): This armor reduces your RP by 3, but does not reduce your evasion and dodge.
    • Fortress (20 points): Reduces the Initiative penalty by 1 and the Evasion/Dodge penalty by 2, but it also reduces the movement speed by 5ft.

data.name: Armor (Light)
data.description:
Increases your Guard by 1 and your Block by 4, but reduces your Initiative by 1 and your Evasion and Dodge by 2.

Mods:

  • A mods
    • Agile Weave (35 points): No armor penalty, but no guard/block bonus. You gain +1 evasion (but no additional dodge). This also takes up your Frame mod slot.
    • Acrobat's Harness (10 points): You gain +10 bonus to athletics while wearing this armor.
    • Camo (10 points): Pick a color theme. You gain +5 to stealth when hiding in environments of that theme, but -5 when hiding elsewhere. A GM may approve new environments, defaults are: green camo (jungle, woodland, prone in grass), yellow camo (desert, savannas), white camo (snow, arctic), dark camo (night, caves, rocky terrain), blue camo (rivers or oceanic)
    • Porcupine Hide (10 points): Enemies grappling you take 1d6 full pierce damage. When escaping a grapple, you also deal 1d6 full pierce damage to the creature grappling you.
  • B mods
    • Sleek (25 points): If you spend RP dodging an attack of opportunity, you may dodge any other attacks of opportunity made in reaction to the same action at the first for free.
    • Padded (25 points): Increase guard vs light attacks by 1, doesn't affect heavy damage.
    • Mistweave (50 points): You no longer provoke attacks of opportunity, but all attacks against you gain Half Pierce.

data.name: Armor Plates
data.description:
Can be attached to an armor to increase its guard, but make it bulkier.

Gives the armor they are attached to +1 Guard (and +2 block), but increases the Burden of it by 3.

Attaching it or removing it from an armor takes 10 minutes.

Can be used together with other armor modifications. Can be put on regular clothing, but always requires an armor proficiency to have an effect. While you can wear multiple armor plates, the effect does not stack.

Despite being craftable by an armorsmith, the item cannot be modified during crafting.

  • Tamahagane
    • Clim Cost per ingot: 1050 Clim
    • Unit cost per ingot: 2000 Tamahagane units.
    • Effect: +1 stat bonus
    • When using Tamahagane to craft an item, you must spend 1 of Tamahagane. If crafting a medium armor or great shield, you must add 1 ingot of Iron. If crafting a heavy armor, you must add 3 ingots of Iron.
  • Mithril
    • Clim Cost per ingot: 4050 Clim
    • Unit cost per ingot: 8000 Mithril units.
    • Effect: +1/+1 stat bonus
    • When using Mithril to craft an item, you must spend 1 ingot of Mithril. If crafting a medium armor or great shield, you must add 1 ingot of Iron. If crafting a heavy armor, you must add 3 ingots of Iron.
  • Orichalcum
    • Clim Cost per ingot: 8050 Clim
    • Unit cost per ingot: 16000 Orihalcum units.
    • Effect: +2/+1 stat bonus
    • When using Orihalcum to craft an item, you must spend 1 ingot of Orihalcum. If crafting a medium armor or great shield, you must add 1 ingot of Iron. If crafting a heavy armor, you must add 3 ingots of Iron.
  • Escudo
    • Clim Cost per ingot: 11550 Clim
    • Unit cost per ingot: 23000 Escudo units.
    • Effect: +2/+2 stat bonus
    • When using Escudo to craft an item, you must spend 1 ingot of Escudo. If crafting a medium armor or great shield, you must add 1 ingot of Iron. If crafting a heavy armor, you must add 3 ingots of Iron.

Stat bonuses:

Armor: Each stat bonus gives a +1 evasion and dodge Material bonus or a +1 guard and +2 block Material bonus. A mithril or primehide armor would thus give +1 evasion, dodge and guard as well as +2 Block.
Shield: Each stat bonus gives a +1 Gear bonus to Dodge or a +3 Gear bonus to Block. 

Armorsmithing Base Leather Materials

The base material for crafting clothing, light armor and cloaks is Animal Hides. Animal Hides must be converted into Tanned Animal Hide before they can be used.

IMPORTANT: Clothing does not gain material bonuses when made out of something better unless they have the “Reinforced Clothing” A mod.

  • Animal Hide:
    • Clim Cost per tanned hide: 300 Clim
    • Unit cost per tanned hide: 500 Animal Hide units
    • Effect: None
    • When using animal hides to craft an item, you must spend 1 tanned animal hide for clothing, light armor, bags and cloaks.

Outside of animal hides, there are a variety of special materials that an armorsmith can use while crafting. These are more expensive, but grant stat bonuses.

  • Direhide:
    • Clim Cost per tanned hide: 1050 Clim
    • Unit cost per tanned hide: 2000 Direhide units
    • Effect: +1 stat bonus
    • When using direhides to craft an item, you must spend 1 tanned direhide for clothing, light armor and cloaks.
  • Primehide:
    • Clim Cost per tanned hide: 4050 Clim
    • Unit cost per tanned hide: 8000 Primehide units
    • Effect: +1/+1 stat bonus
    • When using primehides to craft an item, you must spend 1 tanned primehides for clothing, light armor and cloaks.
  • Dragonscale:
    • Clim Cost per tanned hide: 8050 Clim
    • Unit cost per tanned hide: 16000 Dragonscale units
    • Effect: +2/+1 stat bonus
    • When using Dragonscales to craft an item, you must spend 1 tanned Dragonscale for clothing, light armor and cloaks.
  • Astrahide:
    • Clim Cost per tanned hide: 11550 Clim
    • Unit cost per tanned hide: 23000 Astrahide units
    • Effect: +2/+2 stat bonus
    • When using Astrahide to craft an item, you must spend 1 tanned Astrahide for clothing, light armor and cloaks.

Stat bonuses:

Armor: Each stat bonus gives a +1 evasion and dodge Material bonus or a +1 guard and +2 block Material bonus. A mithril or primehide armor would thus give +1 evasion, dodge and guard as well as +2 Block.

Armorsmithing Special Materials

  • Spidersilk (500 Clim / 15 Crafting Points):
    • Unit cost: 1000 Spidersilk units
    • A Spidersilk armor reduces the Initiative penalty by 1 and the Evasion/Dodge penalty by 2, but the wearer takes double damage from Fire damage. Light armor only.
  • Electrum (3050 Clim / 30 Crafting Points): 
    • Unit cost per ingot: 6000 Electrum units.
    • Armors infused with Electrum gain  a +1 Guard and +4 block bonus against attacks made by Divines, Summons and Otherworlders.
  • Silver (1050 Clim / 30 Crafting Points): 
    • Unit cost per ingot: 2000 Silver units.
    • Silver infused armors remove a Fiend's regeneration. When a fiend hits you with a melee attack or a physical contact attack, they lose their regeneration until the start of their next turn.
  • Mycelite (1550 Clim / 20 Crafting Points):
    • Unit cost per ingot: 3000 Mycelite units.
    • Mycelite infused armor incur 1 less burden to a minimum of 1.
  • Adamantite (2050 Clim / 20 Crafting Points):
    • Unit cost per ingot: 4000 Adamantite units
    • Adamantite armors cannot be destroyed or damaged by effect such as Sunder by non adamantite tools or weapons.
  • Luxaeterna (1550 Clim / 30 Crafting Points): 
    • Unit cost per ingot: 3000 Luxaeterna units.
    • Armor infused with Luxaterna gives the wearer 5 damage reduction against Holy damage.
  • Corvuskite (1550 Clim / 30 Crafting Points): 
    • Unit cost per ingot: 3000 Corvuskite units. 
    • Armor infused with Corvuskite gives the wearer 5 damage reduction against Dark damage.
  • Arcanium (1550 Clim / 30 Crafting Points): 
    • Unit cost per ingot: 3000 Arcanium units. 
    • Armor infused with Arcanium gives the wearer 5 damage reduction against Arcane damage.
  • Vivinthal (1550 Clim / 30 Crafting Points): 
    • Unit cost per ingot: 3000 Vivinthal units. 
    • Armor infused with Vivinthal gives the wearer 5 damage reduction against Water damage.
  • Glacite (1550 Clim / 30 Crafting Points): 
    • Unit cost per ingot: 3000 Glacite units. 
    • Armor infused with Glacite gives the wearer 5 damage reduction against Frost damage.
  • Salachar (1550 Clim / 30 Crafting Points): 
    • Unit cost per ingot: 3000 Salachar units. 
    • Armor infused with Salachar gives the wearer 5 damage reduction against Fire damage.
  • Sylphsteel (1550 Clim / 30 Crafting Points): 
    • Unit cost per ingot: 3000 Sylphsteel units. 
    • Armor infused with Sylphsteel gives the wearer 5 damage reduction against Wind damage.
  • Fulgarite ( 1550 Clim / 30 Crafting Points):
    • Unit cost per ingot: 3000 Fulgarite units. 
    • Armor infused with Fulgarite gives the wearer 5 damage reduction against Lightning damage.
  • Ghimslag (1550 Clim / 30 Crafting Points): 
    • Unit cost per ingot: 3000 Ghimslag units. 
    • Armor infused with Ghimslag gives the wearer 5 damage reduction against Earth damage.
  • Crystal Core (3500 Clim / 35 Crafting Points)
    • Unit cost: 1 core
    • Armor infused with the core of a specific fiend. The wearer may spend 1 Mana and 0 RP to absorb the energy of an elemental (Arcane, Fire, Water, Wind, Earth or any of its subtypes) damage attack. Their next weapon attack gains bonus damage equal to the attacker’s power and becomes the element of the triggering attack.
  • Nullite ( 2050 Clim / 20 Crafting Points):
    • Unit cost per ingot: 4000 Nullite units
    • Anti-Magic Layer: Against spells, you gain 2 guard, 2 evasion and a +2 bonus to saves. However you can no longer become the target of friendly spells (including your own).
  • Runesteel ( 1050 Clim / 10 Crafting Points):
    • Unit cost per ingot: 2000 Runesteel units
    • Select Magic Absorption: Friendly spells targeting you gain +20ft range.
  • Sunsteel ( 1550 Clim, 15 crafting points):
    • Unit cost per ingot: 3000 Sunsteel units
    • Sun Protection: You are immune to any negative effects suffered from being in the sun.
  • Perfect Shell (2000 Clim)
    • Can be made into light armor or armor plates by a Master Armorer (counts as Mithril in terms of difficulty).
    • If used for light armor, the light armor cannot have another special material (may still have flamelon mods) and cannot have frame mods, but it receives +1 guard and +4 Block and may have one medium armor property. Counts as a base material for crafting as well.
    • If used for armor plates, the armor plates receive an additional 2 block for a +1 guard and +4 block total.

Armorsmithing Cloak Materials

Cloaks may benefit from higher base materials being used. This is on a per cloak basis and is listed with the material.

  • No special material
    • A cloak made with no special material may gain a Gear bonus to its Dodge or Block.
    • When made with Direhide/Primehide/Dragonscale/Astrahide gives a +1/+2/+3/+4 Gear bonus to Dodge or a +3/+6/+9/+12 Gear bonus to Block.
  • Night Wolf Pelt (550 Clim / 5 Crafting Points)
    • Unit cost: 1000 units
    • A cloak of night wolf pelt gives the wielder +5 bonus to stealth checks during the night or in area's without light.
    • When made with Direhide/Primehide instead gives a +10/+15 bonus.
  • Fae Wolf Pelt (1050 Clim / 10 Crafting Points)
    • Unit Cost: 2000 Units
    • A cloak of faewolf pelt gives the wielder the ability to spend 4 AP to hide in plain sight. This hide lasts until you take any other action or speak.
    • When made with Primehide, reduce the AP cost to 3.
  • Astral Tiger Pelt (1050 Clim / 10 Crafting Points)
    • Unit Cost: 2000 Units
    • A cloak of astral tiger pelt gives the wielder the ability to teleport when attacked. After an attack against you misses (or you dodge it), you may spend 1 RP to teleport up to 20ft.
  • Wonderland Rabbit Hide (1550 Clim / 15 Crafting Points) (By CCeles)
    • Unit Cost: No units, just 1 hide.
    • When you take a movement action that costs RP, that movement is increased by 5ft. (Doesn't stack with Compact Ergonomics mod)
    • When made with Primehide, the movement is increased by 10ft instead.

data.name: Artifice Limb
data.description:
An artifice item that replaces a lost limb or body part. Each of these must be custom made for a person. When attached, it allows the user to function as if the artifice limb was a normal limb.

Mods

  • A mods:
    • Grapple Launcher (Arm only)(10 points): Allows the user to install a grappling hook artifice in the arm, functioning just like the grappling hook would. (Grappling hook must be supplied separately and takes an errand action from an artificer to install). A grappling hook installed in the arm takes burden like usual and still takes an AP to activate, but requires no AP to pull out.
    • Zoom In (Eye only)(20 points): You may spend 1 AP to gain a +10 bonus to your perception until the start of your next turn.
    • Weapon Slot (Arm only)(20 points): Allows the user to install a weapon into the arm, functioning just like the weapon would (takes an errand from artificer to install). The weapon costs burden like normal, but may be drawn or sheathed for 0 AP once per turn.
    • Movement Burst (Leg only) (20 points): You may spend 0 AP to gain +20ft movement until the start of your next turn. Afterwards, your movement speed is halved until you put in a new shell into your leg.
  • B mods:
    • Blast Knuckle (Arm or Leg only) (25 points): After making a Heavy unarmed attack with the limb, you may spend 0 RP to make a Light attack against all enemies in a 15ft wide, 15ft long cone behind the target. After doing this, you must put in a new shell into the limb to use it again (your movement speed is halved if your leg is unusable).
    • Rocket Punch (Arm only) (50 points): Once per round, you may make a basic unarmed Heavy attack with this limb to a target within 60ft.
    • Thermal Fusion Sight (Eye only)(80 points): Adds thermal vision up to 120ft. This cannot detect things hidden by magical means.  The sight can not discern a difference in heat once something reaches freezing temperatures.

data.name: Artifice Water Purifier
data.description:
A filter that purifies water to make it safe to drink. The device is easy to use and can filter up to 2 liters of water in 1 minute.  

Mods

  • A mods:
    • Quick Filter (10 points): Can filter up to 4 liters of water in 1 minute.
  • B mods:
    • Natural Use (25 points): When used during a rest action, the filter provides half the food needed for a basic rest (20u) provided a camping kit is set up.

data.name: Artificer Materials
data.description:
The base material for crafting items with Artificing is Iron Artifice parts.  You can either buy Iron Artifice parts or convert them from Iron by using the Artificer or Transmuter abilities.

Artifice weapons follow special rules. Weapon attachments follow the regular artifice rules however.

Iron:
Equal artifice parts to the base clim cost of the artifice is required to craft Iron Artifices.

Outside of iron, there are a variety of special materials that an Artificer can use while crafting. These are more expensive, but grant additional C mod slots to the artifice.

You need Artifice Parts of the matching type to craft and the amount you need is determined this way:

(Special Material Modifier) x (Base Clim Cost) = Amount of Special Material Artifice Parts Needed

  • Iron Artifice Parts
    • Multiplier: 1x
    • Effect: 1 C mod slot
  • Tamahagane Artifice Parts
    • Multiplier: 1x
    • Effect: 2 C mod slots
  • Mithril Artifice Parts
    • Multiplier: 2x
    • Effect: 3 C mod slots
  • Orichalcum Artifice Parts
    • Multiplier: 2x
    • Effect: 4 C mod slots
  • Escudo Artifice Parts
    • Multiplier 3x
    • Effect: 5 C mod slots

Artificing Weapon Materials:

The base material for crafting weapons such as pistols or sniper rifles with artificing is Iron. Iron units must be converted into an ingot before they can be used.

  • Iron:
    • Clim Cost per ingot: 300 Clim
    • Unit cost per ingot: 500 Iron units
    • Effect: None
    • When using Iron to craft an item, you must spend 1 ingot.

Outside of iron, there are a variety of special materials that an artificer can use while crafting. These are more expensive, but grant stat bonuses.

NOTE: When making an Artifice weapon that is an actual weapon and not an attachment, you must spend an additional iron artifice parts equal to the cost of the weapon - 500 rather than an extra ingot. This also applies to guns.

  • Tamahagane
    • Clim Cost per ingot: 1050 Clim
    • Unit cost per ingot: 2000 Tamahagane units.
    • Effect: +1 stat bonus
    • When using Tamahagane to craft an item, you must spend 1 ingot of Tamahagane.
  • Mithril
    • Clim Cost per ingot: 4050 Clim
    • Unit cost per ingot: 8000 Mithril units.
    • Effect: +1/+1 stat bonus
    • When using Mithril to craft an item, you must spend 1 ingot of Mithril.
  • Orichalcum
    • Clim Cost per ingot: 8050 Clim
    • Unit cost per ingot: 16000 Orihalcum units.
    • Effect: +2/+1 stat bonus
    • When using Orihalcum to craft an item, you must spend 1 ingot of Orihalcum.
  • Escudo
    • Clim Cost per ingot: 11550 Clim
    • Unit cost per ingot: 23000 Escudo units.
    • Effect: +2/+2 stat bonus
    • When using Escudo to craft an item, you must spend 1 ingot of Escudo.

Stat bonuses depend on if the crafted item is a tool or weapon.

Weapon: The Material bonuses to go Focus and Power. With getting a +1 bonus or a +2/+1 bonus, the crafter may choose which of the two stats gets the extra bonus.

Artificing special materials

  • Dark Iron (550 Clim / 15 Crafting Points) :
    • Unit cost per ingot:  1000 Dark Iron units.
    • Strikes with Dark Iron infused weapons cause the target to be unable to teleport until the end of their next turn.
  • Silver (1050 Clim / 30 Crafting Points):
    • Unit cost per ingot: 2000 Silver units.
    • Dealing damage with Silver infused weapons disables the Regeneration effect of Fiends until the start of your next turn.
  • Electrum (3050 Clim/ 30 Crafting Points):
    • Unit cost per ingot: 6000 Electrum units.
    • Strikes with Electrum infused weapons grant a +2 Electrum Power bonus against Divines, Summons or Otherworlders.
  • Mycelite (1550 Clim / 20 Crafting points)
    • Unit cost per ingot: 3000 Mycelite units.
    • Mycelite infused weapons incur 1 less burden to a minimum of 1
  • Obsidian Steel (550 Clim)
    • Unit cost per ingot:  1000 Obsidian Steel units.
    • Obsidian Steel infused weapons cannot be the targets of magical effects.
  • Adamantite (2050 Clim / 20 Crafting points)
    • Unit cost per ingot: 4000 Adamantite units
    • Adamantite weapons cannot be destroyed by non adamantite tools or weapons.
  • Luxaeterna (1550 Clim / 15 Crafting points)
    • Unit cost per ingot: 3000 Luxaeterna units.
    • Changes the physical damage type into Holy.
  • Corvuskite (1550 Clim / 15 Crafting points)
    • Unit cost per ingot: 3000 Corvuskite units.
    • Changes the physical damage type into Dark.
  • Arcanium (1550 Clim / 15 Crafting points)
    • Unit cost per ingot: 3000 Arcanium units.
    • Changes the physical damage type into Arcane.
  • Fulgarite ( 1550 Clim / 15 Crafting points )
    • Unit cost per ingot: 3000 Fulgarite units
    • Changes the physical damage type into Lightning.
  • Vivinthal (1550 Clim / 15 Crafting points)
    • Unit cost per ingot: 3000 Vivinthal units.
    • Changes the physical damage type into Water.
  • Glacite (1550 Clim / 10 Crafting points)
    • Unit cost per ingot: 3000 Glacite units.
    • Changes the physical damage type into Frost.
  • Salachar (1550 Clim / 15 Crafting points)
    • Unit cost per ingot: 3000 Salachar units.
    • Changes the physical damage type into Fire.
  • Sylphsteel (1550 Clim / 15 Crafting points)
    • Unit cost per ingot: 3000 Sylphsteel units
    • Changes the physical damage type into Wind.
  • Ghimslag (1550 Clim / 15 Crafting points)
    • Unit cost per ingot: 3000 Ghimslag units.
    • Changes the physical damage type into Earth.
  • Nullite ( 2050 Clim / 30 Crafting Points):
    • Unit cost per ingot: 4000 Nullite units
    • All attacks made with this weapon gain the Shieldbreaker property.
  • Runesteel ( 1050 Clim / 10 Crafting Points):
    • Unit cost per ingot: 2000 Runesteel units
    • This weapon can channel spells as if it was a channeling weapon.
  • Sepsium ( 2050 Clim / 30 Crafting Points):
    • Unit cost per ingot: 4000 Sepsium units
    • When damaging a creature with this weapon, they cannot recover HP (except for regeneration type effects) until the start of your next turn.
  • Sunsteel ( 1550 Clim / 15 Crafting Points):
    • Unit cost per ingot: 3000 Sunsteel units
    • Attacks with this weapon gain Full Pierce against creatures weak to light or sunlight.

description.html:
• Dark Iron (550 Clim / 15 Crafting Points) :
    • Unit cost per ingot:  1000 Dark Iron units.

    • Mycelite infused weapons incur 1 less burden to a minimum of 1

    • Obsidian Steel infused weapons cannot be the targets of magical effects.
  • Adamantite (2050 Clim / 20 Crafting points)
    • Unit cost per ingot: 4000 Adamantite units
    • Adamantite weapons cannot be destroyed by non adamantite tools or weapons.
  • Luxaeterna (1550 Clim / 15 Crafting points)
    • Unit cost per ingot: 3000 Luxaeterna units.

  • Sylphsteel (1550 Clim / 15 Crafting points)
    • Unit cost per ingot: 3000 Sylphsteel units
    • Changes the physical damage type into Wind.

    • Unit cost per ingot: 3000 Ghimslag units.

    • Unit cost per ingot: 4000 Nullite units

    • Unit cost per ingot: 2000 Runesteel units

data.name: Artificer's Kit
data.description:
Artificer’s Patch kit with various tools for maintaining artifices.

Rest Action: You can either patch a broken, non-airship Artifice (with the exception of Aerial Staves), allowing it to be usable until the end of the scenario if its repairable. The Artifice still counts as broken at the end of the scenario and cannot be patched again until fully repaired.  Alternatively, you can instead choose to create an Artifice Shell, paying its cost in Magical Fuel to create.

data.name: Astra Guidance Beacon
data.description:
While this artifice is in effect, the spirit core values of your allies within 300ft of you are treated as 500 higher than they actually are for the purposes of calculating astra corruption risks. Does not stack with similar resistance boosting effects and only works on allies with a Spirit Core lower than yours.

Mods

  • A mods:
    • Increased Effect (20 points): Now boosts the spirit core values of your allies by 1000 instead of 500.
  • B mods:
    • Exousiai Protection (80 points): You and allies affected by this device ignore 1 level of astra corruption increase caused by Exousiai type fiends.

data.name: Axe (One-Handed)
data.description:
Wild Swing: When attacking a target, you still deal 4 (Light Attack) or 8 (Heavy/Precise Attack) damage if the attack misses. This is reduced by guard (to a minimum of 1). On damage effects do not trigger from this damage.

Mods

  • A mods:
    • Reinforced Langet (10 points): This weapon cannot be disarmed.
    • Bearded Extension (20 points): Wild Swing now ignores guard, but the damage is reduced to 2 (light attack) or 4 (heavy attack).
    • Rotational Stability (35 points): If a target moves away from you when you attack with this weapon and your next attack this turn is a throwing attack using this weapon against that target, that attack gains lock on.
  • B mods:
    • Boomerang Wing (25 points): After using a throwing attack with this weapon, you can return the weapon to your hand for 0 RP.
    • Lancebreaker (80 points): You gain a +2 Lancebreaker Power bonus against enemies wielding polearms or lances.

data.name: Binoculars
data.description:
Binoculars let you zoom in on distant views, bringing faraway details up close and clear. 

When using these, you gain a +10 bonus on perception checks against things further than 60ft away but a -10 penalty to things within 60ft.

Mods

  • A mods:
    • Quick Focus Dial (20 points): The penalty for things within 60ft is reduced from -10 to -5.
    • Night Mode (20 points): Looking through the binoculars gives you Nightvision up to 120ft.
  • B mods:
    • Range Finder (25 points): When looking through this item, you can tell how far objects are from you.
    • Anti-Illusion Lens (50 points): You gain a +10 bonus to determine if something is an Illusion or not.
