data.name: Twinblade (Two-handed)
data.description:
Twin Strike: You can make dual wield attacks as if you were wielding two weapons.

Mods

  • A mods:
    • Haladie Blade (20 points): Attacks with this weapon have -1 Power, but you can make 2 offhand attacks per turn instead of one.
  • B mods:
    • Shadow-Type Saber (80 points): When engaged in melee and you take a block or dodge action and then you are attacked by another melee attack by a different enemy, you may use block or dodge against that attack for 0 RP.  Applies once per turn

data.name: Universal Armor Mods
data.description:
Base Mods:

These are mods that can be put on any armor (not shield), regardless of type. The crafting cost to add these is listed after the name.

A mods:

  • Ceremonial Armor (10 points): You gain +10 bonus to negotiation and intimidation checks, but automatically fail any stealth checks.
  • Cast Off Design (10 points): After using the Block action, you may spend 0 RP to cast off the armor immediately unequipping it. The armor becomes Broken until repaired.
  • Hidden Armor (10 points): This armor looks like normal clothing to other creatures (which may make you look more vulnerable than you are).
  • Ki Concealment (20 points): Requires Manaweave Frame mod. While wearing this armor you gain presence concealment. Spending any mana immediately removes presence concealment. After losing presence concealment, you can’t regain it until you rest for the day.

B mods:

  • Mana Barrier (25 points): Requires Manaweave Frame mod. While putting on this armor, your mana and max mana is set to 0. For each mana you lose thanks to this effect, you gain 7 temporary HP. When you would regain mana or HP from resting, this temporary HP regenerates (up to a max of what you started with at the start of the arc)
  • Sensory Suit (50 points): This armor boosts the range of Mind Connection and Scry by 10x.  Also reduces the mana cost of Psychometry by 1.

Frame mods:

  • Barrier (20 points): This armor provides no passive guard bonus, but reduces the Initiative penalty by 2 and the Evasion/Dodge penalty by 4. When taking the Block action, you still receive the normal bonus the armor would provide.
  • Protective Coating (20 points): Reduces the Initiative penalty by 1 and the Evasion/Dodge penalty by 2, but only gives the passive guard increase. When taking the Block action, it does not gain an increased guard (though any other bonuses to your Block such as your Toughness still apply).
  • Manaweave (20 points): Reduces the Initiative penalty by 1 and the Evasion/Dodge penalty by 2. but reduces the wearer's current and maximum mana by 3 when equipped. Cannot be equipped if it would reduce the mana below 0.

Flamellon Mods:

Flamellon mods are special mods that can be put on armors. To put one of these mods on an item you must have sufficient items with the matching Flamelic Polarity.

Adding a layering of the required element automatically fulfills gives polarity equal to the units in the ingot. For example, adding a Salachar ingot as layering also gives you 3000 Salachar polarity.

  • Arcanium
    • Quick Channel Layer (B mod, 40 points, 2000 Arcanium Polarity): Your maximum mana is increased by 1 while wearing this armor.
  • Salachar
    • Fire Armor (Frame mod, 20 points, 600 Salachar Polarity): Reduces the Initiative penalty by 1 and the Evasion/Dodge penalty by 2, but you take double damage from Water damage.
    • Refractory Plates (A mod, 35 points, 1000 Salachar Polarity): You become immune to Burning and natural heat effects.
    • Sunfire Infusion (B mod, 80 points, 4000 Salachar Polarity): All creatures ending their turn next to you take Light Fire damage.
  • Sylphsteel
    • Turbulent Air Layer (Frame mod, 20 points, 600 Sylphsteel Polarity): Reduces the Initiative penalty by 1 and the Evasion/Dodge penalty by 2, but the bonuses of this armor only apply against ranged attacks.
    • Wind's Blessing (B mod, 25 points, 1250 Sylphsteel Polarity): After you Dodge, you gain +10ft of movement speed until the end of your next turn.
    • Cloud Pillow (B mod, 25 points 1250 Sylphsteel Polarity): When you would take falling or pushback damage, you treat the distance you would fall as 30ft lower.
    • Aerolevitation Effect (B mod, 80 points, 4000 Sylphsteel Polarity): You may Hover.
  • Fulgarite
    • Lightning Armor (Frame mod, 20 points, 600 Fulgarite Polarity): Reduces the Initiative penalty by 1 and the Evasion/Dodge penalty by 2, but you take double damage from Earth damage.
    • Static Armor (B mod, 25 points, 1250 Fulgarite Polarity): Anyone ending their turn next to you is afflicted with Static 12 that triggers at the end of their next turn.
    • Franklin Badge (B mod, 50 points, 2500 Fulgarite Polarity): Any attack dealing Lightning damage that targets an ally within 30ft of you and doesn’t include you as a target suffers a -5 penalty to Accuracy.
    • Lightning Reprisal (B mod, 80 points, 4000 Fulgarite Polarity): The first time each round you take damage from a Heavy attack in melee, you may make a Light attack against the attacker.
  • Corvuskite
    • Shadow Buoyancy (Frame mod, 20 points, 600 Corvuskite Polarity): Reduces the Initiative penalty by 1 and the Evasion/Dodge penalty by 2 during the night.
    • Light Absorbing Layer (A mod, 10 points, 300 Corvuskite Polarity): You gain +5 stealth during the night (doesn’t stack with cloak).
  • Vivinthal
    • Condensation Layer (Frame mod, 20 points, 600 Vivinthal Polarity): Reduces the Initiative penalty by 1 and the Evasion/Dodge penalty by 2, but you take double damage from Lightning damage and you are considered permanently soaked.
    • Bubble Flow Armor (B mod, 25 points, 1250 Vivinthal Polarity): You gain a swim speed of 20ft and can hold your breath for twice as long.
    • Galilean Latticing (B mod, 25 points, 1250 Vivinthal Polarity): You may walk on water as if it was normal ground.
    • Fog Plates (B mod, 80 points, 4000 Vivinthal Polarity): You gain a +4 bonus to your Dodge.
  • Glacite
    • Ice Armor (Frame Mod, 20 points, 600 Glacite Polarity): Reduces the Initiative penalty by 1 and the Evasion/Dodge penalty by 2, but you take double damage from Fire damage.
    • Permafrost Mantle (B mod, 50 points, 2500 Glacite Polarity): Enemies within 5ft of you are slowed. This slow is applied during a movement if they walk within 5ft of you. Lasts until they are no longer within 5ft of you, but it applies for the entire movement if leaving the range.
  • Ghimslag:
    • Seismographic Reflex Layer (B mod, 50 points, 2500 Ghimslag Polarity): You gain 20ft of Tremorsense.
    • Rock Plates (B mod, 80 points, 4000 Ghimslag Polarity): You gain a +8 bonus to your Block.
  • Luxaeterna:
    • Luxflow Coating (A mod 20 points, 600 Luxaeterna Polarity): You radiate a bright light that illuminates up to 60ft away.
    • Triboluminescent Plates (B mod 80 points, 4000 Lux Aeterna Polarity): Undead creatures that deal damage to you take Light Holy damage in return.
  • Aetherplumes (feathers/wings with high magic concentration.  Tengu/Harpy/Fae etc):
    • Tengu Armor (A mod 35 points, 1000 Aetherplume Polarity): Your movement speed increases by 5ft while hovering or flying.
    • Aerodynamic Glider (A mod 35 points, 1000 Aetherplume Polarity): You may spend 1 RP to glide (as per the aeromancer ability)
  • Phoenix Materials (Phoenix Core):
    • Trauma Heat (B mod 80 points, 4000 Phoenix Polarity): Once per round, when you drop to 0 or lower HP while above 0 HP, you may immediately revive at 1 HP. You still gain an injury.
  • Gravity Materials (Gravity Orb):
    • Repulsive Sheeting (A mod 35 points, 1000 Gravity Polarity): When you push or pull a target, you may push or pull them for an additional 5ft.
    • Anti-Terror Field (B mod 50 points, 2500 Gravity Polarity): You gain a +4 bonus to your evasion against ranged attacks, but you cannot make any ranged attacks yourself (they automatically miss).
  • Plant (Ygdrassil Seed):
    • Dryad Bark (A mod 35 points, 1000 Plant Polarity): You can move through natural difficult terrain without losing movement.
    • Resinosis (B mod 50 points, 2500 Plant Polarity): When you take the Block action against an enemy attack, you heal for 3 HP.
  • Silver:
    • Ionic Field (B mod 25 points, 1250 Silver Polarity): Your astra corruption resistance is increased by 1.
  • Insectoid (Fae Cicada Shell):
    • Hive Mind (A mod 35, 1000 Insectoid Polarity): You gain a +1 to initiative for every allied creature (including yourself) wearing an armor with this mod (max +3).
    • Bee Armor (B mod 50 points, 2000 Insectoid Polarity): The first time each combat you take damage from an attack, the attacker becomes Dazed as bees attack it.
    • Living Armor (B mod 80, 4000 Insectoid Polarity): The first time each combat you take damage from a melee attack, you release a swarm of insects in a 5ft radius around you. The swarm remains in the same spot and any creature other than you ending its turn inside of it takes 6 full pierce damage.
  • Undead (Soulstone):
    • Reanimated Bone (B mod 25 points. 1250 Undead Polarity): When you are downed, attacks against you do not gain Full Pierce as your armor actively protects you.
    • Hands of Ptah (B mod 25 points, 1250 Undead Polarity): While you are downed, a necromantic hand activates on your armor, performing emergency medical aid, you regain 2 HP per turn.
    • False Bone Layer (B mod 80 points, 4000 Undead Polarity): Critical hits against you do not gain Full Pierce (but still do max damage)
  • Spidersilk:
    • Slippery (B mod 25 points, 1250 Spidersilk Polarity): You automatically escape from the first grapple effect against you each encounter. 
    • Sticky (B mod 50 points, 2500 Spidersilk Polarity): You gain Spider Climb while wearing this armor (as per spiderfolk racial)
  • Poison Materials (Toxic Core)
    • Poison Inlay (B mod 25 points, 1250 Poison Polarity): You may apply a poison to this armor as a Rest action. When you are hit by a melee attack, the poison explodes outwards and automatically triggers on the attacker as if you had dealt damage to them.
    • Poison Resistance (B mod 50 points, 2500 Poison Polarity): You gain 5 DR against Poison damage.

data.name: Universal Artifice Mods
data.description:
Base Mods:

These are mods that can be put on any artifice, regardless of type. The crafting cost to add these is listed after the name.

A mods:

  •  

B mods:

  •  

C mods:

  • Double Barrel (10 points): The artifice can hold up to 2 shells. You still reload 1 shell at a time.
  • Triple Barrel (10 points): The artifice can hold up to 3 shells. You still reload 1 shell at a time. Requires Double Barrel on the artifice.
  • Quadruple Barrel (10 points): The artifice can hold up to 4 shells. You still reload 1 shell a time. Requires Triple Barrel on the artifice.
  • Quintuple Barrel (10 points): The artifice can hold up to 5 shells. You still reload 1 shell a time. Requires Quadruple Barrel on the artifice.
  • Advanced Melding (10 points): The burden cost of this artifice is reduced by 1, to a minimum of 0, if you have at least 1 other artifice with this mod in your combat burden. Only takes effect once, even with 3+ items with this mod. Does not work on artifice weapons that are their own weapon already, such as power gauntlets.
  • Superior Melding (10 points): The burden cost of this artifice is reduced by 1, to a minimum of 0, if you have at least 1 other artifice with this mod in your combat burden. Only takes effect once, even with 3+ items with this mod. Does not work on artifice weapons that are their own weapon already, such as power gauntlets. Requires Advanced Melding mod on the artifice.
  • Perfect Melding (10 points): The burden cost of this artifice is reduced by 1, to a minimum of 0, if you have at least 1 other artifice with this mod in your combat burden. Only takes effect once, even with 3+ items with this mod. Does not work on artifice weapons that are their own weapon already, such as power gauntlets. Requires Superior Melding mod on the artifice.

data.name: Universal Crafting Mods
data.description:
A mods:

  • Cross Peen Hammer (30 points): When crafting two of the same one-handed weapon with the same mods and materials, you may use double materials and only use one crafting attempt to make a pair of weapons.
  • Westrian Style Tool (10 points): You no longer roll dice and instead take 5 for every d10 crafting roll.
  • Sylvan Style Tool (20 points): While crafting points are 30 or less, you gain a +1 bonus to your crafting rolls. 
  • Kiraran Style Tool (30 points): You may reroll any one dice when crafting immediately after determining the result.

B mods:

  • Expertise (80 points): You gain a +1 bonus to crafting checks with a specific armor group, weapon group (or tools) or any other valid expertise.

data.name: Universal Translator
data.description:
A small black box. 

When a creature speaks into it while activated, everyone who hears the creature’s voice can automatically understand what they are saying, regardless of the language they are speaking in. 

It cannot translate for creatures that lack a proper language such as animals.

Mods

  • A mods:
    • Parley Mode (20 points): The device now translates all words spoken near it, allowing for easier two way communication.
  • B mods:
    • Voice Amplification (50 points): In addition to translating, the speaker's voice is also amplified to be heard from over long distances as if shouting.

data.name: Universal Weapon Mods
data.description:
Base Mods:

These are mods that can be put on any weapon, regardless of type. The crafting cost to add these is listed after the name.

While gathering is a universal mod, you still cannot gather unless the weapon is a tool that can be used for gathering.

A mods:

  • Ninja Weapon (10 points): This weapon is treated as a weapon that can be used for Ninjutsu.
  • Quickdraw (10 points): You may draw this weapon for 0 AP.
  • Gathering (35 points): This weapon gives a +1 bonus to gathering rolls its used in.
  • Perfect Balance (20 points): When using the weapon in dual wielding, you can perform a dual wield attack with your other weapon, even when making a heavy or precise attack with this weapon.
  • Surprise Weapon (35 points): The weapon is designed to look like a mundane object.  Each Combat, after you draw the weapon, if the next attack you make that round is using this weapon and is a basic light or heavy attack it gains the Trick Attack keyword.  After benefitting from this bonus, you cannot do so again the same combat even if drawing a different weapon with with Surprise Weapon or Hidden Weapon.
  • Versatile (10 points): Can be added to a 1h weapon from a group that also has an option to be a 2h weapon (ie Axe, but not small weapons). Increases the burden of the weapon by 1, but the weapon can be used as either a one-handed or two-handed weapon. Must declare which version you are using at the start of your turn, before you making any attacks with this weapon.

B mods:

  • Perfect Edge (25 points): An accuracy roll of 20 gains Sure Hit. If you roll a 20 and choose to have this apply, any Full Pierce is removed from the attack.
  • Momentum (25 points): After downing or killing an enemy, you may Sidestep up to your speed towards another enemy as part of that action.
  • Gathering II (80 points): This weapon gives a +1 bonus to gathering rolls its used in. Stacks with Gathering mod.

Alloy Mods:

Alloy mods can also be put on any weapon, but require the weapon to include a specific type of alloy. If the weapon does not include this alloy, the mod cannot be used.

  • Arcanium
    • Barrier Weaving (A mod, 20 points): When you apply a Shield to an ally or yourself, your shield is treated as if the stat it scales off is 1 higher. (If it doesn’t scale off a stat, there is no effect)
  • Salachar
    • Burning Weapon (B mod, 50 points): The first basic attack made with this weapon each round inflicts Burning 18 to the target on damage until the start of your next turn.
  • Ghimslag:
    • Slowing Weapon (B mod, 50 points): The first basic attack made with this weapon each round slows the target on damage until the start of your next turn.
  • Fulgorite:
    • Thundering Weapon (B mod, 25 points): The first basic attack made with this weapon each round inflicts Static 18 to the target on damage.
    • Conductor (B mod, 50 points):  When this weapon deals Lightning damage against a soaked target, it gains Half Pierce.
  • Luxaeterna:
    • Shining Weapon (A mod, 10 points): Your weapon emits a bright light in a 60ft radius. Can be enabled or disabled for 1 AP.
    • Healer Weapon (A mod, 20 points): When you heal an ally or yourself, you heal as if your power (or focus, agility or toughness if the heal scales off those) was 1 higher.
    • Undead Slayer (B mod, 50 points): When this weapon deals holy damage, it always deals Full Pierce damage against undead unless the undead resists Holy damage.
    • Shielding Healer (B mod, 50 points): When you cast a healing spell that costs mana, the target(s) of your spell gain Temporary HP equal to your Toughness until the start of your next turn.
  • Sylphsteel:
    • Pushing Weapon (B mod, 25 points): The first basic attack made with this weapon each round pushes the target back 10ft on damage.
  • Corvuskite:
    • Stealth Weapon (B mod, 25 points): The first attack of an encounter does not break stealth if made with this weapon.
    • Darkness Weapon (B mod, 80 points): If the first basic attack on your turn made with this weapon deals damage, you may immediately hide from the target (but not other enemies) even if you’re not in cover.
  • Glacite
    • Slowing Weapon (B mod, 50 points): The first basic attack made with this weapon each round slows the target on damage until the start of your next turn.

Flamellon Mods:

Flamellon mods are special mods that can be put on weapons. To put one of these mods on an item you must have sufficient items with the matching Flamelic Polarity.

  • Aetherplumes (feathers/wings with high magic concentration. Tengu/Harpy/Fae etc):
    • Aerial Supremacy (A mod, 30 points, 1500 Aetherplume polarity): You gain +1 accuracy against flying creatures.
    • Aerial Takedown (B mod, 50 points, 2500 Aetherplume polarity): If you damage a flying creature and it would lose altitude from taking damage, the altitude they lose is doubled.

description.heading: Base Mods:
description.html:
These are mods that can be put on any weapon, regardless of type. The crafting cost to add these is listed after the name.

While gathering is a universal mod, you still cannot gather unless the weapon is a tool that can be used for gathering.

description.heading: A mods:
description.html:
• Ninja Weapon (10 points): This weapon is treated as a weapon that can be used for Ninjutsu.
  • Quickdraw (10 points): You may draw this weapon for 0 AP.
  • Gathering (35 points): This weapon gives a +1 bonus to gathering rolls its used in.
  • Perfect Balance (20 points): When using the weapon in dual wielding, you can perform a dual wield attack with your other weapon, even when making a heavy or precise attack with this weapon.
  • Surprise Weapon (35 points): The weapon is designed to look like a mundane object.  Each Combat, after you draw the weapon, if the next attack you make that round is using this weapon and is a basic light or heavy attack it gains the Trick Attack keyword.  After benefitting from this bonus, you cannot do so again the same combat even if drawing a different weapon with with Surprise Weapon or Hidden Weapon.
  • Versatile (10 points): Can be added to a 1h weapon from a group that also has an option to be a 2h weapon (ie Axe, but not small weapons). Increases the burden of the weapon by 1, but the weapon can be used as either a one-handed or two-handed weapon. Must declare which version you are using at the start of your turn, before you making any attacks with this weapon.

description.heading: B mods:
description.html:
• Perfect Edge (25 points): An accuracy roll of 20 gains Sure Hit. If you roll a 20 and choose to have this apply, any Full Pierce is removed from the attack.
  • Momentum (25 points): After downing or killing an enemy, you may Sidestep up to your speed towards another enemy as part of that action.
  • Gathering II (80 points): This weapon gives a +1 bonus to gathering rolls its used in. Stacks with Gathering mod.

description.heading: Alloy Mods:
description.html:
Alloy mods can also be put on any weapon, but require the weapon to include a specific type of alloy. If the weapon does not include this alloy, the mod cannot be used.

  • Arcanium
    • Barrier Weaving (A mod, 20 points): When you apply a Shield to an ally or yourself, your shield is treated as if the stat it scales off is 1 higher. (If it doesn’t scale off a stat, there is no effect)
  • Salachar
    • Burning Weapon (B mod, 50 points): The first basic attack made with this weapon each round inflicts Burning 18 to the target on damage until the start of your next turn.
  • Ghimslag:
    • Slowing Weapon (B mod, 50 points): The first basic attack made with this weapon each round slows the target on damage until the start of your next turn.
  • Fulgorite:
    • Thundering Weapon (B mod, 25 points): The first basic attack made with this weapon each round inflicts Static 18 to the target on damage.
    • Conductor (B mod, 50 points):  When this weapon deals Lightning damage against a soaked target, it gains Half Pierce.
  • Luxaeterna:
    • Shining Weapon (A mod, 10 points): Your weapon emits a bright light in a 60ft radius. Can be enabled or disabled for 1 AP.
    • Healer Weapon (A mod, 20 points): When you heal an ally or yourself, you heal as if your power (or focus, agility or toughness if the heal scales off those) was 1 higher.
    • Undead Slayer (B mod, 50 points): When this weapon deals holy damage, it always deals Full Pierce damage against undead unless the undead resists Holy damage.
    • Shielding Healer (B mod, 50 points): When you cast a healing spell that costs mana, the target(s) of your spell gain Temporary HP equal to your Toughness until the start of your next turn.
  • Sylphsteel:
    • Pushing Weapon (B mod, 25 points): The first basic attack made with this weapon each round pushes the target back 10ft on damage.
  • Corvuskite:
    • Stealth Weapon (B mod, 25 points): The first attack of an encounter does not break stealth if made with this weapon.
    • Darkness Weapon (B mod, 80 points): If the first basic attack on your turn made with this weapon deals damage, you may immediately hide from the target (but not other enemies) even if you’re not in cover.
  • Glacite
    • Slowing Weapon (B mod, 50 points): The first basic attack made with this weapon each round slows the target on damage until the start of your next turn.

data.name: Wand (One-Handed)
data.description:
Magic Blast: You may alter the damage type fired by an attack made with this weapon for 0 AP. The damage type must be an element type you have mastered (usually unlocked through classes) or one that’s built into the weapon. Each weapon has at least one element built in.

Range: 60ft

Mods

  • A mods:
    • Ornamental (10 points): You may use this weapon as one minor item such as an instrument or parasol.
    • Echo Blast (20 points): When you make a basic Heavy attack, you may split the damage against two different targets in range. Make only 1 accuracy check against both.
    • Warding Wand (35 points): You may spend 1 AP to gain 5 temporary HP until the start of your next turn.
  • B mods:
    • Dedicated Focus (50 points): Gain +1 bonus to accuracy rolls, but can only fire elemental attacks of 1 element. Spells cast through this wand only gain that bonus if they deal that element of damage.
    • Mana Core (80 points): When you deal max damage with an attack made with this weapon or with a spell cast through this weapon against an enemy in an encounter, your next spell this turn costs 1 less mana (min 0)

data.name: Whip (One-Handed)
data.description:
Whip Crack: You gain +5ft range on your weapon attacks. Weapon attacks made at max range (default of 10) gain +1 damage. Your threatened range is still 5ft.

Mods

  • A mods:
    • Barbed Wire (10 points): Upon landing a critical hit with this weapon, apply Bleeding to the target.
    • Fluttering Ribbon (35 points): At the start of your turn, you may change your threatened range to 5-10ft until the start of your next turn.
  • B mods:
    • Binding Flow (50 points): When dealing damage with a Heavy attack, you may choose to not do damage to instead reduce a creature’s movement speed to 0 until the start of your next turn or until you move. Does not work against bosses or creatures bigger than you.
    • Hooked Coil (80 points): When dealing damage with an attack of opportunity against an enemy leaving your range, you may pull them back 5ft. Only triggers once per turn.

data.name: Wind Bubble
data.description:
A simple device that can be attached to the body or held in the hand. When activated, it creates a bubble of wind around the wielder that slows down falling speed to 40ft per round. If the wearer reaches the ground while in this bubble, they take no fall damage.

Mods

  • A mods:
    • Quick Activation (20 points): The activation cost is reduced by 1 AP or 1 RP, to a minimum of 0.
  • B mods:
    • Slow Fall (25 points): Reduces the falling speed down to 20ft per round.
    • Underwater Mode (50 points): If used underwater, the bubble provided you air as you slowly float upwards.

data.name: Winged Backpack
data.description:
A backpack that looks ordinary at a first glance. It can store the same amount of items as a normal backpack. When activated, a pair of mechanical wings fold out. While the wings are out, you slow down your falling speed to 15ft per round and you are able to move horizontally as if normally moving. If you hit the ground while they are active, you do not take any falling damage. Lasts for 5 minues or until you hit the ground.

Mods

  • A mods:
    • Quick Activation (20 points): The activation cost is reduced by 1 AP, to a minimum of 0.
  • B mods:
    • Hover Mode (80 points): When activated, the wearer can fly at half speed up to a maximum of 40ft high. If activated when higher than 40ft high, you glide down until you reach the 40ft height limit. Functions similarly to the Flight ability in regards to taking damage while flying.

data.name: Wyvern
data.description:
A wyvern trained to be ridden by people.

 

Stats:

HP: 75

Focus: 4

Power: 6

Agility: 3

Toughness: 6

Speed: 40ft

Size: Large

 

Special qualities:

Flying Mount: Your mount can fly. While flying you may only move in a straight line when making a movement action. While moving only on the ground, your speed is reduced to 20ft but this restriction does not apply.

In flight vulnerability: When your mount takes damage while flying, its height is lowered by 20ft. If this would reduce its height to the ground level, it becomes rooted and cannot fly again until the end of your next turn.

Breath Weapon: You may spend 1 AP to make your mount use a breath weapon (damage type dependent on the wyrm type), making a Light attack against all enemies in a 30ft cone. This attack uses your mount’s stats instead of your own

data.name: Acolyte's Journey
data.benefit1: You gain proficiency in light armor, shields and a single common group of weapons. This group may include Channeling Weapons, even though they aren't consider common weapons. (But you only get 1 of the possible channeling weapons).
data.benefit2: You gain +5 skill points in the Religion skill. You can exchange any skill point for 2 expertise points, but must spend them in this skill.
data.benefit3: You are welcome at establishments for your religion and they are obligated to help you with lodging, advice, food and sometimes equipment.
data.benefit4: Upon Mastery of the class, you gain Elemental Mastery in your chosen Divine's element (or Holy if just human).

data.name: Alarm Ward
data.description: A ward that can be placed on a normal-sized room or can be combined to ward off a house or larger area. Each ward can cover a 40ft radius. For each Alarm Ward placed in the same area as another Alarm Ward, this radius increases by 40ft (For example, 120ft with 3 Alarm Wards). If someone other than you passes through the ward, the ward triggers creating a loud ringing noise that persists until the ward is disabled. Casting this takes 10 minutes of uninterrupted casting. Once triggered, the field remains active for 5 more minutes before vanishing. At the time of casting, you may choose people that can pass through the barrier without triggering it. If not triggered, Alarm Ward lasts until you remove it. For each Alarm Ward you maintain, your maximum mana is reduced by 1. This is considered a tier 1 ward.

data.description:
Masterful Dilution
Cost: 40 Crafting Points
Description: 
By diluting the contents to the perfect required amounts, you gain an additional Elixir, Potion, Flask, Potion or Salve upon crafting success. Stacks with Efficient Dilution.

Distillation
Cost: 40 Crafting Points
Description: 
You extract the highest quality healing materials from herbs, granting Healing +8 to a Potion with a heal or shielding effect.

Explosive Lining
Cost: 10 Crafting Points
Description: 
You carefully add an alchemical compound to a pressurized Flask. If the Flask has an area of effect, increases the area by another 5ft (example a 10ft radius becomes 15ft radius).

Purify Elixir
Cost: 40 Crafting Points
Description: 
You reduce the toxicity of an Elixir that has been detoxified while still maintaining its effect, reducing the damage from taking an Elixir by an additional 5.

data.name: Allow me to clean that~
data.description:
You instantly remove a negative effect from the terrain (such as Oil Slick, Sheet Ice, Web etc). Permanent effects such as fissure or effects with HP like a wall cannot be removed with this. A maximum of 15x15ft can be removed in 1 use and you may move to any spot of the cleaned terrain afterwards.

data.name: Arcane Barrier
data.description:
You create a Magical Barrier that absorbs damage until it breaks. The barrier has HP equal to 15 + your Focus. The barrier has a Guard of 0 and any damage it takes is subtracted from the barrier’s HP. When the barrier breaks, any remaining damage is subtracted from your HP. The barrier otherwise lasts until the start of your next turn or until you take any action other than the Block action.

This spell does not provoke attacks of opportunity and does not protect against true damage.

data.name: Biohacking
data.description:
At the start of an arc, you can transmute a gene from a Chimera Subrace into your DNA as long as you have a sample (a vial of blood).

Transmuting the gene does not consume the item. Add a single Chimera gene to your gene inventory. 

You can perform this action again for an IP or EP. Biohacking can store genes equal to your gene limit.

data.name: Blackbird
data.description:
You deploy a Blackbird, a small artifice drone that outputs a grainy image to a device on your wrist.  The blackbird has a maximum range of 3000ft and can observe major movements and structures such as doors and enemies.  The drone cannot display fine movements or detail such as words in a book without being up close, but can see large signs.  The blackbird is the size of a walnut and is relatively quiet, and can only be heard by those with normal human hearing within 10 ft.

The fuel shell lasts for one flight, up to 15 minutes.  If your Blackbird is lost or damaged, you must create a new one as an errand action before you can use this again.

data.name: Blood Frenzy
data.description:
You go into a blood frenzy, mindlessly attacking enemies near you.

While the blood frenzy lasts, you must attack the nearest enemy target with a basic unarmed attack. If two targets are equally close, you may choose which one you attack. If no enemies are within range, you must use your movement to move closer to the closest visible enemy until you can attack them.

While under the effect of blood frenzy, you heal for half the damage you deal with your unarmed attacks.

You cannot use Vampire Bite while under the effect of Blood Frenzy.

This effect lasts until all visible enemies are dead or until your mana runs out. At the start of your turn, you lose 2 mana.

data.name: Bunshin Tai no Jutsu
data.description:
You create a body double of yourself that has the same stats you do at the time of creation. You and the body double share the same HP, Mana, AP and RP etc and unless stated otherwise your clones are considered you. All effects on you are mirrored on your clone and vice versa, however a clone cannot benefit from Presence Concealment.

When taking an action, you may choose to let the user be yourself or the body double. However, the body double may only use basic abilities and abilities with the Ninjutsu keyword and cannot create more body doubles of itself. 

When you take the movement action or use a non-teleport movement ability, your clone may move for the same amount of distance as you moved.

You may spend 0 AP or 1 RP to dismiss the body double. A clone can never travel more than 300ft from your actual body, but while it lasts you may spend 2 AP to swap locations with it.

A clone lasts until you rest.

data.name: Channel Eidolon: Distracting Swarm
data.description:
You summon a distracting swarm around a target. The target immediately loses any Concentration effects and suffers -5 penalty to Perception checks unless they spend 1 RP to sidestep out of the effect. If they did not move, they also cannot use any abilities with the Concentration keyword until they move.

You can only have 1 Distracting Swarm active at the same time.

data.name: Channel Eidolon: Draw Luck
data.description:
You draw on your luck, manipulating the circumstances around you to the best possible state. If you are the target of an attack, that attack becomes a 1. If you made a roll, that roll becomes a 20 (despite the pact cost). 

May also be used in situations that don’t have you making a roll, such as flipping a coin, but the act that you’re influencing cannot take more than 5 seconds to complete.

After using this ability, you become temporarily afflicted with bad luck. The GM decides what exactly happens and what triggers it, but it could turn your roll into a 1, make an enemy roll a 20 against you or something related to the environment. After a bad luck action happens, the bad luck is removed.

You cannot use this ability again until after the bad luck has been removed.

data.name: Channel Eidolon: Vine Wall Cover
data.description:
Thick vines sprout from the ground or natural wall as you create a 5x5 wall of vines that is 10ft high. The wall of vines counts as full cover (unless you peek from it) and has HP equal to your Toughness x6. The vines are sturdy enough to stand on.

Lasts for up to 5 minutes and you can only have 5 instances of Vine Wall Cover at one time.

You can create a Chemical Explosive during an interlude phase for free, but can only carry one at a time. The check to disable a Chemical Explosive is equal to 20 + 2 x Power of the creator.

data.name: Combat Chemistry
data.description:
Can only be used once per encounter. 

Using your knowledge of alchemy, you jury-rig a special item that has the effect of an an elixir, poison, flask or potion with a cost of 300c or lower. 

You can only make the base version of the item with no mods. The item doesn't take up burden, but must be used before the start of your next turn or it is lost. This item can only be used by you.

data.name: Conduit
data.description:
When Mind Connection is active, you can channel some abilities through others with Mind Connection. You cannot use conduit with abilities that require a physical object to be present, such as a Mystic Eye power or a specific weapon or abilities that require you to interact with a physical object, such as Snatch. Abilities that require your physical body to make an attack, such as Double Punch also don't work.

You still must pay the costs to use the abilities, and your Mind Connection source becomes the origin point of the spell for purposes of range. Abilities with a range of Self cannot be used through Conduit.

Any ability used through Conduit that isn't an Aetherie ability costs +1 AP (or RP) to use.

data.name: Corpse Domination
data.description: You raise the target under your command. A target raised in this way is treated as a non-heroic unit that takes its own actions, however it will try to act in a way that is most helpful to you in the fight. The raised target keeps all of its stats and abilities it had in life, though it only starts with half its maximum health (before any reductions) and whatever mana it had left over when it died. This summon lasts until the end of the encounter or until its HP reaches 0, upon which it immediately dies again and cannot be raised again in any way.

data.name: Counterspell
data.description:
You pay RP equal to half the AP spent on the triggering Spell (rounded up) or equal to the RP spent on the triggering spell and Counter it, canceling its effect without refunding the AP. If the AP cost is higher than your RP, you cannot Counterspell it. 

If used against a non-Grunt target, you must pay 1 mana for each point of Focus that the target has more than you (minimum 0). 

This Spell does not provoke attacks of opportunity, but cannot be used to Counter Spells that have an AP and RP cost of 0.

data.name: Craft Artificer's Glove
data.description:
You create a personalized Artificer’s Glove that only you have proficiency with.  Choose a glove type with properties of your choosing at the time of creation.  You can modify this glove for an errand action to change the property, but you can only have one property at a time and only one Artificer’s glove at a time.

Gamma Glove (Hacker): Artifice Jamming. For 1 RP you can Jam a small shell artifice within 120ft causing it to malfunction and be unusable until the user spends 1 AP to clear the jam.

Sigma Glove (Combat Artificer): Heat Sink.  0 RP, 1 mana.  Your glove emits frost energy that saps heat from an artifice, allowing it to bypass the once per turn limit a single time. Overcharge: 1 RP, the mana cost becomes 0.

Delta Glove (Specialist):  The glove is specialized for an expertise skill granting you +10 in that skill.  For instance, it might fire an arcane blast to propel you, granting you +10 to jumping. May not choose artisan or gathering skils.

data.name: Craft Pemmican
data.description:
Errand. You turn up to 1000u of food into 25 Pemmican Bars (40u of food per bar), which are incredibly shelf stable and easy to eat.  They perform about the same as Military Rations but they are wrapped by special leaves that deter pests—useful and consistent adventure food.

You may also use this as an IP action to convert up to 2000u of food into 50 Pemmican bars.

data.name: Create Talisman
data.description:
You may create a talisman or scroll by spending an interlude point. Choose an Spell that you know or choose a specialized talisman, such as a Sealing Talisman. You inscribe that Spell onto a piece of paper. A talisman of a Spell allows you to use the Spell at a different time. When you use it, it is consumed. A Spell talisman costs as much AP and mana to use as the original Spell does. 

You may craft up to 5 talismans per interlude point. A secret art talisman takes up 3 of these slots. When crafting, you may make no more than 2 of the same spell. A crafted talisman costs 1 burden to carry with you. A Secret Art talisman costs 2 burden and can only be used through the Secret Talisman ability.

Crafting a talisman costs 100 calligraphy units per AP and Mana of the spell. A spell with no AP or Mana costs 50 units. If the spell has an RP cost and no AP cost, it costs 200u per RP. If the spell has a casting time longer than 4 AP (ie 10 minutes), then treat the spell as having a cost of 4 AP.

Some spells, such as Summon Lesser Eidolon and Summon Eidolon may be unavailable.

At any point of the line you can draw a second 55ft long perpendicular line centered on that point of the initial line. You make another Light attack against all caught on this second line and on damage you inflict Illumination X where X is your Focus / 2 (Rounded Down) until the end of your next turn.

If a target gets hit by both lines, the second line deals Heavy damage and inflicts your full Focus in Illumination instead.

data.name: Culinary Basics
data.description:
Mushroom Stock
Cost: 15 Crafting Points
Description: 
Turns a Gourmet Base Stock into a Mushroom Stock (does not stack with other stocks), which when added to a cooked meal gives a +1 Focus Food Bonus that lasts for 24 hours. Requires 1 Box of Fresh Mushrooms. 

Meaty Stock
Cost: 15 Crafting Points
Description: 
Turns a Gourmet Base Stock into a Meaty Stock (does not stack with other stocks), which when added to a cooked meal gives a +1 Power Food Bonus that lasts for 24 hours.  Requires 1 Box of Fresh Meat.

Fish Stock
Cost: 15 Crafting Points
Description: 
Turns a Gourmet Base Stock into a Fish Stock (does not stack with other stocks), which when added to a cooked meal gives a +1 Toughness Food Bonus that lasts for 24 hours.  Requires 1 Box of Fresh Fish.

Vegetable Stock
Cost: 15 Crafting Points
Description: 
Turns a Gourmet Base Stock into a Vegetable Stock (does not stack with other stocks), which when added to a cooked meal gives a +1 Agility Food Bonus that lasts for 24 hours.  Requires 1 Box of Fresh Vegetables.

Spicy Stock
Cost: 30 Crafting Points
Description: 
Turns a Gourmet Base Stock into a Spicy Stock (does not stack with other stocks), which when added to a cooked meal gives a +1 Crafting Food Bonus that lasts for 24 hours.  Requires 1 bundle of Spicy Peppers.

Herbal Stock
Cost: 30 Crafting Points
Description: 
Turns a Gourmet Base Stock into a Herbal Stock (does not stack with other stocks), which when added to a cooked meal gives a +1 Gathering Food Bonus that lasts for 24 hours. Requires 1 bundle of Fresh Cooking Herbs. When gathering from a node with a bonus from this stock, you keep the benefit for that entire node unless you go a day without harvesting from that node.

Stir Layered Flavors
Cost: 30 Crafting Points
Description: 
Allows you to add another flavor, allowing you to add a second different flavor.  Choose from Mushroom, Meaty, Fish, Vegetable, Spicy or Herbal—then add the corresponding ingredient.  For example:  A Mushroom stock + Meaty stock becomes a Mushroom-Meaty stock that grants +1 Power / +1 Focus Food Bonus.  

Use Every Last Drop
Cost: 15 Crafting Points
Description:  
Increases the stock yield by 2.

Secret Ingredient
Cost: X Crafting Points
Description: 
You mix a special material into the stock.  Each material has its own crafting point cost.

Create Box or Bundle of Food
Cost: Errand.
Description: 
You create a perfect mix of ingredients that would be worthy of a stock with 500u of matching material.  Example:  500u of Meat can make 1 Box of Fresh Meat.  You can make 5 boxes of any kind for one errand action.

data.name: Deconstruction
data.description:
By spending an Interlude Point, you deconstruct a basic item into materials. You gain 500 matching crafting material per ingot or block used in the item. If the item does not use ingots, you instead get 1 matching crafting material per clim value of the item.

Regardless of the material used in the item, you will only gain the base price amount even if using upgraded materials and all alloys and upgrades are lost.  You can deconstruct up to 5 basic items for 1 interlude point.

Alternatively instead of 1 basic item, you can transmute up to 1000u of random junk into up to 250u of usable basic (ie: Iron, Pine etc) Blacksmithing Materials, Armorsmithing Materials, Carpentry Materials, Calligraphy Material, Magical Fuel Materials or Medical Materials units at a 4:1 ratio.

You can also use Deconstruction as an Errand Action, but the deconstruction limit is reduced to 1 basic item instead of 5 basic items.

data.name: Delay Time
data.description:
You choose one or more negative effects on the target that would trigger at the start or end of their turn. They trigger on the turn after the turn they would normally trigger instead. 

You may only delay an effect once, but you are able to delay Stasis even though the target is normally immune to all abilities.

Start of turn effects still trigger at the start of the turn and end of turn effects still trigger at the end of the turn.

data.name: Destroy Ground
data.description:
You destroy natural earth with magical speed, creating up to a 10ft x 10ft x 10ft hole in most natural earth. Those caught in the effect may spend 1 RP to Sidestep 5ft out of the effect. All caught in the effect fall down 10ft into the hole and take falling damage as normal.

The spell requires natural ground to be below the touching surface to function. It may work on the bottom floor of a house, but will fail if used higher up or in some dungeons

data.name: Dirge of Despair
data.description:
All enemies within range must make a save against your Potency or become affected by this Song. While affected, you may subtract 1d4 from a single roll they make until the start of your next turn. You may choose to add this after seeing the roll.

Upkeep: At the start of your next turn and every turn thereafter, you may spend 1 AP to continue this performance. Enemies that successfully made their save, do not have to save again against this continued performance, but those who were affected continue to be affected.

data.description:
When you use this ability you choose one of the following effects:

 

Divine Protection: You are protected from harm through divine protection, gaining 100 damage reduction against the next source of damage you take.

Fortune: When used for this effect, this ability becomes Instant. You may reroll your last d20 and take the new result.

Health: You heal someone (or yourself) within touching distance for 15 hp.

Light: You summon a bright light at your position that shines a bright light up to 30ft around you. You may detonate this light by spending 0 AP to Daze all enemies within its range.

 

Once you use this ability, you may not use it again until after a rest.

data.name: Divine Release
data.description:
Demons can feed on their own lifeforce to release a brilliant display of divine powers. Horns can elongate, fangs might grow, eyes glow and even wings can sprout as the Demon realizes their Divine Roots.

Upkeep: 11 HP

You transform into your new form and take 11 true damage. You may end this form at any time by spending 0 RP. While the form lasts you gain the following benefits:

Fallen Guard: When you take the Block basic action, you gain an additional +5 to guard.
Fallen Alacrity: You gain +5 movement speed and the ability to fly.
Fallen Might: You gain +1 AP at the start of your turn.
Fallen Conviction: When you are reduced to 0 HP, you do not enter the downed state. You still receive the wounded status. While at or below 0 HP, the upkeep for this ability is increased to 16. If you end this ability while at or below 0 HP, you are immediately placed into the downed state. If your HP become equal to or lower than your negative maximum HP, you are immediately incapacitated and this ability ends.

Once you use this ability, you cannot do so again until you finish an interlude rest phase.

data.name: Dragon Breaks The Ranks
data.description:
You gain Flight and surround yourself in fire, then Sidestep to a point in a direct line. You destroy low cover you pass through, though the GM may rule that some cover is too sturdy to be destroyed. In either case, you continue until you reach the target and may make a single melee Heavy Attack against an enemy in range with your weapon. Any other characters in your path may spend 1 RP to move 5ft out of your charge or take Light Fire Damage.

If you have an element mastered, you may change the Fire damage of this ability to the element you have mastered.

This spell does not provoke attacks of opportunity.

data.name: Dullahan's Mount
data.description:
You conjure up a black horse that becomes part of you. You immediately mount when using this ability and upon dismounting, the horse vanishes. While mounted, your movement speed is increased by 30ft and you are considered a large creature, but you may only move in a straight line. When attempting to move through 5ft wide spaces, it is considered difficult terrain for you. You also suffer a -10 penalty to most finesse athletics checks as well as climbing and swimming checks while mounted.

Any attack against the horse is considered an attack against you instead. As the horse is considered part of you, any displacement or teleport abilities move the horse alongside with you. You may dismount by spending 0 AP.

data.name: Duplicate
data.description:
You attempt to analyze the spell and duplicate it. After the triggering spell resolves, immediately cast a copy of it. You must select a valid target for this copy, pay any additional mana cost originally on the spell as well as pay any costs that are not AP or RP. Failure to do so will make the duplicated spell fizzle, dissipating the magic harmlessly into the air.

Upon successfully copying the spell, it resolves with the same damage and effects as the original spell, though using your stats to resolve them.

The cost is 1 RP for a 0-2 AP spell or 2 RP for a 3-4 AP spell. Spells with a higher cost cannot be duplicated.

Secret Arts and Esoteric Arts also cannot be duplicated and upon attempting to do so, this ability is canceled and any cost refunded. Unique spells by heroic or boss enemies may also be impossible to duplicate (GM's discretion).

data.name: En-dama
data.description:
You throw a smoke bomb on the ground within range that blocks line of sight in a 5ft radius (15x15 area total) of where it was thrown. Targets inside or within 5ft of the smoke can only see up to 5ft into or out of the smoke.

If you’re inside of it at the point it's thrown, you may immediately gain the Hiding state from anyone you have cover or concealment from.

The smoke lasts until the start of your next turn. When it ends, if you are inside your smoke, you may immediately move up to your speed and you are considered hidden up until you finish that movement. If you end your movement in cover, you keep being Hidden from people you have cover from.

data.name: Explosive Ward
data.description: A ward that can be placed on a door or medium-sized container of some sort. If other than you knowingly tries to open the door or container in any way (whether normal opening, attacking it etc), the ward triggers creating a loud noise and dealing Heavy Fire Damage to all creatures in a 10ft radius around the container. All items inside the container (if any) also take this damage. Once triggered, the bounded field vanishes. Casting this takes 10 minutes of uninterrupted casting. You may at the time of casting choose a number of people equal to your Focus that can also open the container or door without triggering the ward. If not triggered, Explosive Ward lasts until you remove it. For each Explosive Ward you maintain your maximum mana is reduced by 2. This is considered a tier 2 ward.

data.name: Fae Knight Style: Willow Stance
data.description:
You enter Fae Knight Style: Willow Stance. Increasing your Fluttering Blade Limit to 2. Shields can be used as Fluttering Blades while in Willow Stance. 

For 2 mana, all Fluttering Blades created in Willow Stance this turn can be enhanced with Heavy Spin, allowing them to be used for some Willow abilities but they no longer gain your agility as extra evasion.  Heavy Spin blades also deal 5d6 upgraded heavy attack damage, even if they were originally a one-handed weapon.

When directing your Heavy Spin blades to move, you may direct two blades for 1 AP instead of just 1 blade.

data.name: Faerie Light Eyes:  Empty
data.description:
You lock eyes with an enemy, casting an illusion onto the target’s mind. Name an ability that the target had previously used in the current encounter. The target forgets the target ability, being unable to use it completely while the Illusion is in effect. This ability cannot target Secret Arts, Climax Arts or Esoteric Arts. Only one target may be under the effect of this illusion at a time. If the target is non-heroic and under the effect of Faerie Light Eyes: Hold Person, instead the target immediately is rendered insane permanently. An insane target takes no further combat actions.

If used on a grunt under the effects of Hold Person, they do not need to meet the normal requirements for this ability.

Does not work against Boss type enemies. Some abilities such as those granted by items, passives or racial abilities (such as flight) also cannot be removed by this ability (GM's discretion).

data.name: Farming Basics
data.description:
Spiritual Ground
Cost: 1 Interlude Point
Description: 
You infuse the land with your spiritual energy, creating up to 10 plots of land suitable for farming. These plots of lands can grow food and herbs at an accelerated rate and allow the planting of tier 1 rare herbs.

All plots of land must be filled with seeds before they begin growing. 

After creating a spiritual ground, you may immediately use Sow Seeds in it for 0 IP.

You can only have 1 spiritual ground at the same time.

Sow Seeds
Cost: 1 Interlude Point
Description: 
You may plant seeds in plots of land. You may plant 1 set of seeds in each plot of land you can work.

Harvest
Cost: 1 Interlude Point
Description: 
You harvest the planted seeds or take care of the plants not ready to be harvested yet. Do a crafting session. Your crafting score is the total value of seeds you can harvest or take care of.

If your crafting score is not high enough to harvest or take care of all seeds you planted, you must give up on some of the seeds. Starting from the seed with the highest difficulty, you drop seeds until your total crafting score matches or exceeds the total difficulty of the seeds.

Infuse Qi
Keywords: Rapid
Description: 
You infuse one of the planted herbs with Qi, upgrading it from common to rare and adding 10 to its difficulty.

Bountiful Harvest
Keywords: Rapid
Description: 
You bless one of the planted seeds that grants Food units or Alchemy materials. It grants double that amount and you add 5 to its difficulty. Does not stack.

data.name: Fissure
data.description:
You slam the ground and create a 15ft wide fissure up to the target point. Those at the edges of the spell’s range may spend 1 RP to Sidestep 5ft out of the effect. All caught in the effect fall down 20ft into the fissure and take falling damage as normal.

The spell requires natural ground to be below the touching surface to function. It may work on the bottom floor of a house, but will fail if used higher up or in some dungeons.

data.name: Flame Infusion
data.description: You surround a willing target in searing flames, changing their typing to Fire II. As a Fire II type, they take half damage from Fire and Frost Damage or attacks with the Fire or Frost keywords unless that attack deals true damage. They take 50% more damage from Water Damage or attacks with the Water keyword. While the ward lasts, they also gain immunity to Burning. The ward lasts until the end of the encounter or until their type is overwritten by a more powerful type.

data.name: Flight
data.description:
You gain controlled Flight up to your speed. If you take damage while flying higher than 5ft above the ground, your altitude drops by 20ft. If this would reduce your altitude to the point where you touch the ground, you become rooted and cannot fly again until the end of your next turn. If the attack that reduced your HP came from a flying creature other than yourself, you do not lose altitude.

When you end your turn within 5ft of the ground, Flight ends.

data.name: Fluttering Blade
data.description:
You infuse a melee weapon within ability range that you are familiar with (belongs to you and was originally in your combat inventory at the start of the encounter, or has been in your dimensional storage for at least a day) with magic, causing it to float into the air that listens to your directions. You can have one Fluttering Blade at a time. 

When a Fluttering Blade weapon takes damage, it drops to the ground and becomes inert.

Fluttering Blade has a base evasion of 7+Your Agility.

You can direct your Fluttering Blade to move, it has a base movement speed of 30ft and does not provoke attacks of opportunity by moving. You can also direct your Fluttering Blade to attack within its attack range. It can make basic Heavy, Light and Precise attacks as well as special Fae Knight attacks. The blade is counted as its own entity for the purpose of attacking, though it uses your stats.

You need at least 1 hand free to direct a blade.

If they take damage while flying higher than 5ft above the ground, their altitude drops by 20ft. If this would reduce their altitude to the point where they touch the ground, they become rooted and cannot fly again until the end of their next turn. If the attack that reduced your HP came from an flying creature other than yourself, you do not lose altitude.

data.name: Foretell
data.description:
You receive a vision of the near future. Roll a d20 and store that number. When you or your allies are going to roll that dice type, you can instead replace it with your dice roll, you then lose your Foretell dice. You can only have one Foretell dice at a time, casting Foretell again overwrites the previous dice. Foretel dice last until the end of your next turn.

After rolling, you may spend 1 mana to reroll the dice once. After doing this, you can't do so again for this use of the ability.

data.name: Four Point Strike
data.description:
You may make a Light Attack against the target. On damage, you apply Wave Palm II. 

Combo: If used after Two Point Strike or against a target afflicted with Wave Palm I, the mana cost is reduced by 2 and the AP cost by 1. If the target is afflicted with Wave Palm I, you apply Wave Palm III instead of Wave Palm II.

Wave Palm increases the mana cost of the afflicted target’s next action that uses mana by an amount equal to the amount of stacks applied. If the triggering attack makes the number of total stacks exceed the target's current mana, they lose mana equal to the amount of total stacks and take true damage equal to triple this amount. Wave Palm does not stack with itself, use only the higher value.

If the target has no mana, they immediately take true damage as if their stacks exceeded their current mana.

When the Wave Palm effect triggers, either by increasing the mana cost or by dealing the true damage, the Wave Palm effect is removed.

data.name: G. Shift
data.description:

You temporarily mutate your body, granting an effect similar to one of the following Alchemy Elixirs:  Rabbit, Reaper, Shark, Tunnel, Bull, Bear. This effect does not stack with their corresponding Elixir Effect. This effect cannot be dispelled and lasts until the end of the encounter.

data.name: Gene Activation
data.description:
You transmute yourself, consuming a gene. You transform,  granting yourself a single chimera racial ability that corresponds with the gene. 

You are transformed until the end of your next turn. Doing this consumes the gene from your DNA. You can deactivate the transformation for 0 RP.

You cannot obtain and use abilities that require an IP or EP to use through this ability.
data.requirement: Must have the required Gene in your gene inventory.

data.name: Glacial Bastion
data.description:
You encase yourself in a Glacial Wall that fills your space until the start of your next turn, making you untargetable for attacks during the duration. This Glacial Wall has HP equal to 20 + Focus, any remaining damage is transferred to you (mitigated by your armor).  While encased, you can cast White Thunder on your encased Ice for 1 RP which removes Glacial Bastion. Other than White Thunder, you cannot take any other actions while under the effect of Glacial Bastion.   

This Spell does not provoke attacks of opportunity.

data.name: Gloom Infusion
data.description:
You surround a willing target in gloom and shadow, changing their typing to Dark II. As a Dark II type, they take half damage from Dark Damage or attacks with the Dark keywords, unless the attack deals true damage. They take 50% more damage from Holy Damage or attacks with the Holy keyword. While the ward lasts, they also gain 60 feet Darkvision and a +4 bonus to saves against mind affecting effects. 

The ward lasts until the end of the encounter or until their type is overwritten by a more powerful type.

data.name: Goring Charge
data.description:
You lower your head and charge in a direction with your horns. You move X times your speed in a straight line. If you move at least 15 feet, you make a Heavy attack against the first target in your path. They may sidestep this attack for 1 RP.

If a target sidesteps your attack, you continue charging for your maximum distance or until you hit an object. If you charge into another creature, you make a Heavy attack against them as well and the process continues. You do not provoke attacks of opportunity from creatures that sidestepped your attack for this movement.

If the object you charge into is destroyable, the GM may also ask you to make a Heavy attack against it.

These attacks are considered unarmed attacks that you are proficient in, even if you normally wouldn't be. It does not benefit from any sort of gauntlet bonuses.

You make a Light attack against the target. Afterwards, you gainHardening Fist, which gives +2 guard and +8 Block, but lose 4 evasion (including dodge) until the start of your next turn.

Combo: If used after Steadfast Earth Stance, the mana cost is reduced by 1.

data.name: Harvest Moon
data.description:
You call down a harvest moon over the area that shines in a 60ft radius around yourself. 

All allies in range may spend 2 Mana at the start of their turn to heal for 15 HP.

All enemies starting their turn in its range must make a Save against your potency or become slowed.

You may end this ability early by choosing to make a 0 AP heavy attack against an enemy slowed by this ability. This attack must be made with a Scythe. On killing blow of that attack, you recover 1 mana.

Upkeep: You must spend 1 mana at the start of your turn to continue this effect.

data.name: Heavenly Lightning Stance
data.description:
You enter the Heavenly Lightning Stance, a stance that lets you move with the unpredictability of the heavens. For your first movement of your turn, you may pass through enemies and your movement becomes a Sidestep.

If you have mastered Sky Talon Style, entering this stance also counts as your Wind Stance.

This stance lasts until you enter a different stance or make an attack with anything other than a melee attack or an ability with the Unarmed Strike keyword.

data.name: Hide in Shadows
data.description:
You jump into a target’s shadow. If you were hidden before using this ability, you remain hidden inside the shadow. Else, the target or any other enemy may attack the shadow as if they were attacking you. If you take damage, you are forced out. While you’re inside the shadow, you travel with the target when it moves, including if it teleports, but cannot take actions other than exiting it.

You may exit the shadow willingly for 0 RP. When you exit it, if you were hidden, your next basic attack that turn against the target whose shadow you were hiding in gains Full Pierce.
data.requirement: Must be day.

data.name: Holy Orders
data.description:
You target an enemy unit within range, causing the target to become your Holy Order until the start of your next turn. 

While active, only your Holy Order may be chosen as the target for any offensive ability, or must be included as a target to use an offensive action. 

If you make an attack of opportunity against your Holy Order, or if they move away from you while in your melee range, you can Sidestep up to twice your Speed towards them for 0 RP after their movement finishes.

Can only be used on your turn before you use an offensive action.

data.name: Horse Body
data.description:
You may carry an ally on your back without lowering your movement speed and your Burden is increased by 2. However, you are considered a large creature. When attempting to move through 5ft wide spaces, it is considered difficult terrain for you and many humanoid buildings will struggle to accommodate you. You also suffer a -10 penalty on most finesse athletics checks, as well as a -10 penalty on climbing and swimming checks.

Picking up an ally takes 1 AP and they cannot take AP actions while on your back. You or they may spend 1 AP to dismount and act like normal.

data.name: Human Adaptability
data.description:
As an errand action, you may refund an ability and choose to learn another ability. You cannot pick an ability that makes you ineligible for any of your prerequisites. Your new ability must cost the same as your unlearned one, or you must pay additional normal EXP to make up for the cost difference. If you choose to unlearn a class and learn a new one with this ability, you must spend IP for that new class as normal. Any previous IP spent on learning the class you unlearn is NOT refunded.

If you choose to refund primary stats, secondary stats or skill points and then level up the class again, you must put those points back in the same things you originally put them in.

Does not work on breakthroughs.

data.name: Independent Action
data.description:
Your animal summoned through the Summon Animal ability gains the ability to act independently. It acts at initiative 0, though you may still control its action. A summon with Independent Action starts with 2 AP and 1 RP and may use those as normal. If they have an ability that costs mana, then you still have to pay that mana cost.

While it is under the effects of Independent Action, you cannot command your summon through the use of your own AP.

A summon targeted by this ability takes up 2 slots towards the summon limit. If this would put you past your limit, you cannot use this ability.

data.name: Inexorable Shadow Stance
data.description:
You enter a stance that enhances your attacks at the cost of your own life. Whenever you hit an enemy with an unarmed attack, you may deal Light or Heavy true damage to yourself to increase the damage of the attack by the same amount. This may be done after reactions to the attack have been declared, though an enemy may still choose to react to it again or differently afterwards.

If used with an attack that hits more than 1 target, this extra damage only applies to one of the damage rolls.

You may do this effect twice per round. If an enemy dodges to make you miss and refund the effect, it still counts as one of your uses. When enhanced, these attacks gain the Augment keyword.

This stance lasts until you enter a different stance.

In addition, when you are about to take an action that leads to grave harm or death (example: The enemy has an instant death ability), you can receive a premonition from the DM.

data.name: Lengthened Incantation
data.description:
You lengthen the time it takes to cast your next Spell to empower it. You may add 2 AP to the cost of your next spell with the Spell gaining additional Light Damage on it. If you cannot pay this AP cost this turn, the Spell also gains the Setup keyword.

If the Spell has multiple attack rolls or different damage rolls, this bonus only applies to one of them.

However, if the spell is a Scattering AoE spell then the bonus damage applies to all targets of that spell. If that Scattering spell hits a target more than once it only applies to one damage roll. If the spell lasts for multiple turns, it only applies to the initial casting.

While in this stance, you cannot become the target of allied abilities, except AoE ones that also hit enemies at the same time. At the same time, you cannot use abilities on allies either except damaging ones that also work on enemies.

However, you may use Aid abilities on yourself.

data.name: Lord of Mercenary
data.description:
At the start of a new adventure, you can hire an NPC to help you for the entire adventure. You can also use this ability at other times that the DM allows you to. When you summon them, choose a name and appearance for the character unless the DM does.

The cost is per week and depends on the NPC. If your hired help dies, you cannot use this ability until you complete a new separate adventure. This ability counts as 1 towards your summon limit as long as the mercenary is in your employ, unless specified. These mercs can be modified through Expert Summoner breakthrough, but this must be done the moment you hire them.

Refer to the Monster guide for stats of mercenaries. The mercenaries and costs are:
Archer: 250/ Week
Acolyte: 750c / Week
Tank: 500c / Week
Apprentice: 750c/ Week
Rogue: 200c / Week
Brute: 200c / Week

data.name: Luminous Form Stance
data.description:
You enter the Luminous Form Stance and create the Threads of Light. These manifest spiritual cloth, spectral arms or something similar that enhances your reach.

While in this stance, you gain an additional 10ft range on your unarmed attacks and your threatened range becomes 5-15ft. Whenever you deal damage to an enemy with an unarmed strike ability (not basic attacks), you gain 1 stack of Harmony up to a maximum of 5. You cannot gain more than 1 Harmony per use of ability.

When you leave this stance all stacks are lost.

This stance lasts until you enter a different stance or you willingly move, with the exception of movement abilities with the unarmed strike keyword. Abilities from allies that allow you to move, such as Gravitional Ki, count as willing movement.

data.name: Mage Armor
data.description:
You gain magical Light Armor, Medium Armor or Heavy Armor until the end of the encounter. This function just as normal armor of that type would, giving the same benefits and penalties. Does not stack with other armor, apply the effects of the Mage Armor This magical armor does not require proficiency of any sort and does not cost any Burden to wear and carry.

You may apply the effects of Barrier, Fortress, Manaweave, Protective Coating or Spidersilk to this armor (It must still meet the requirements, you cannot put fortress on a light armor for example). This can only be done when you first apply it, not if you later change your armor during combat.

If Mage Armor is active, you may spend 2 AP to change its type or to remove it.

data.name: Mana Shield
data.description:
You use your Encounter Start action to give yourself Mana Shield, which gives you Temporary HP equal to your Toughness + 3 or Focus + 3 (whichever is higher). 

Wearing armor reduces this to 2/3rd, 1/3rd or 0 if wearing Light, Medium or Heavy Armor respectively. While Mana Shield is active, you do not provoke attacks of opportunity from casting Spells from enemies that are Challenged by you.

Until the end of the encounter, at the start of your turn you may spend 1 mana to restore your Mana Shield to its maximum value. (With similarly reduced values for wearing armor)

If you did not use this as an encounter start, you may also spend 1 AP and 1 Mana to activate this.

A marked target may spend 1 mana per AP/RP of the action (with a minimum of 1 mana even for 0 AP abilities) to temporarily ignore the restricting effect for a movement action.

data.name: Mind Connection
data.description:
You physically touch up to five willing people, granting them Mind Connection—creating a mind link through you.  While linked, each creature can speak through telepathy to all other creatures linked to the same caster.  Mind Connection has unlimited duration but also reduces your maximum mana by 1, this effect lasts until you cancel Mind Connection.  Mind Connection has a maximum range of 500 ft—breaking this range doesn’t cancel the spell but interrupts the signal until within range again.

While Mind Connection lasts, you may spend 1 AP to transfer view through the eyes of one of the people connected with the mind link.

data.name: Mist of the Vale
data.description:
A mist rolls out from around you, trapping those caught in it in a misty vale in which travelers are doomed to die. All in the mist must make a save against your Potency when they try to escape it. If they fail their save when they attempt to move out, you may finish the remaining movement for them as long as they end within your mist. This movement does not provoke attacks of opportunity.

The mist also blocks Line of Sight. Targets inside of or within 5ft of the mist can only see up to 5ft into or out of mist.

The mist is a 15ft radius around yourself, but if flying it does not go below you. You may choose to exclude allies from the trapping effect. If you do, the upkeep mana cost and initial mana cost is increased by 1.

Upkeep: 1 AP

data.name: Move Piece
data.description:
You move a puppet piece you can see that's under your control. The way it moves depends on the type of piece. When a piece moves, it's a Sidestep.

Pawn: Moves up to 2 squares orthogonally or 1 square diagonally in a straight line.

Knight: Moves 1 square orthogonally, then 1 square diagonal in the same direction it moved in orthogonally (like a knight in chess). Can pass through allies and enemies.

Bishop: Moves up to 8 squares diagonally in a straight line. 

Rook: Moves up to 8 squares orthogonally in a straight line.

Queen: Moves up to 8 squares orthogonally or diagonally in a straight line.

Except for the Knight, chess pieces cannot move through allies and stop their movement when they hit an object or creature. If this happens, it makes a Heavy attack that deals Physical(Bludgeoning) damage against that target with your stats. A knight that makes an attack and does not kill the target remains in its original spot.

On damage, a piece is promoted into a higher rank (Pawn -> Bishop/Knight -> Rook -> Queen). A queen cannot promote.

On Killing Blow, a piece occupies the square of the thing it attacked.

data.name: Mud Wall
data.description:
You create a wall 4ft high, 1ft thick and up to 20ft long that serves as low cover. Anybody attempting to get over the wall treats it as difficult terrain. Walls must be placed on solid ground and cannot be stacked on top of eachother.

Each 5ft of wall has 60 HP and dissolves if it reaches 0. It otherwise lasts until the end of the encounter.

You may spend 1 RP instead of 2 AP on this ability instead.

data.name: Past Self
data.description:
You place a past self token at your current position that lasts until the end of the encounter. Your past self tokens are used for other abilities and cannot be attacked normally.

When you make a weapon attack, you may have the attack come from a past self token. After a past self token attacks, it becomes targetable by attacks and effects for 1 round as if you were in that position though you cannot be hit more than once by the same attack because of this.

Your past selves cannot be moved, willingly or forcefully.

data.name: Place Trap
data.description:
You choose to spend either 1 minute or 1 hour to place an undetermined trap in an area. You may only have 2 traps placed at a time in this way.

When an enemy comes within 20ft of you, you may spend 0 RP to determine the effects of a trap and trigger it. If you spent 1 minute, you may choose a Simple Trap. If you spent 1 hour, you may choose either a Simple Trap or a Complex Trap.

Log Swing (Simple): The target takes Light bludgeoning damage and is knocked back 20ft.

Snare (Simple): You place up to 3 snare traps, each within 20ft of each other. When triggered, the target’s movement is interrupted and they fall prone.

Net (Complex): The target is caught in a net and raised up into the air. It remains rooted there until the net is destroyed by dealing 15 damage, after which the target falls prone on the ground below it.

Pitfall (Complex): The target falls down a 5x5, 20ft deep pit and takes falling damage as normal.

A used trap cannot be reused. Setting a trap consumes a Trapper's Trap.
data.requirement: Sufficient time (see description)

data.name: Plume-Treading Art
data.description:
After you use Cloudstep, you treat air as regular walkable terrain until the end of your turn. At the end of your turn, if still standing on air and not Flying, you float back down to the ground without taking fall damage.

In addition, after each AP spent on the Move action or an ability that lets you move, you gain 1 Windflow up to a maximum of 6. Each stack of Windflow gives a +5 Windflow bonus to your movement speed. These stacks last until the end of the encounter or until you end your turn without having moved.

Cloudstep also always gives you 1 stack, up to your normal cap.

data.name: Poison Spore
data.description:
You may spend either 2 AP or 1 RP to use this ability.

You create an Area of Poison Spores around you or the Host of Spore Symbiote. Units who end their turn in the Poison Spore take Full Pierce Poison damage equal to your Power + 2. You and the host of Spore Symbiote are immune to your own Poison Spore. Poison Spore lasts until the end of the encounter but you can only have one instance of Poison Spore active at a time.

The spore stays centered around the original target, even if the target of this ability moves. If the original target of this ability was the symbiote target and you swap the symbiote target, the location of the poison spore moves with it.

data.name: Power Jump
data.description:
You jump up to 60ft vertically straight up into the air.  You can additionally move 5ft horizontally afterwards.  Unless flying, you automatically land straight down from your position at the end of your turn or for 0 AP, this falling movement does not provoke attacks of opportunity and you don’t take fall damage from it. If you land inside an occupied square, you are shunted 5ft into an empty square (your original one if possible).

You cannot make any non-teleport movement actions while in the air unless you’re flying, but can still take other actions (such as attacking) while airborne.
